units.sanskrit: abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭrāya dvāḥstha mām prativedaya dvāḥsthaḥ uvāca viduraḥ ayam anuprāptaḥ rāja indra tava śāsanāt
units.english: Bring him here without delay.' Despatched by Dhritarashtra, the messenger went to Kshatri and said, 'O thou of great wisdom, our lord the mighty king desireth to see thee.' Thus addressed, Vidura (set out and) coming to the palace, spoke unto the orderly, 'Apprise Dhritarashtra of my arrival.' Thereupon the orderly went to Dhritarashtra, and said, O, foremost of kings, Vidura is here at thy command.

units.sanskrit: draṣṭum icchati te pādau kim karotu praśādhi mām
units.english: He wisheth to behold thy feet.

units.sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca praveśaya mahā prājñam viduram dīrghadarśinam
units.english: Command me as to what he is to do.' Thereupon Dhritarashtra said, 'Let Vidura of great wisdom and foresight enter.

units.sanskrit: aham hi vidurasya asya na akālyaḥ jātu darśane dvāḥsthaḥ uvāca praviśa antaḥpuram kṣattar mahā rājasya dhīmataḥ
units.english: I am never unwilling or unprepared to see Vidura.' The orderly then went out and spoke unto Vidura, 'O Kshatri, enter the inner apartments of the wise king.

units.sanskrit: na hi te darśane akālyaḥ jātu rājā bravīti mām vaiśampāyanaḥ uvāca tatas praviśya viduraḥ dhṛtarāṣṭra niveśanam
units.english: The king says that he is never unwilling to see thee.' "Vaisampayana continued, 'Having entered Dhritarashtra's chamber, Vidura said with joined hands unto that ruler of men who was then plunged in thought, 'O thou of great wisdom, I am Vidura, arrived here at thy command.

units.sanskrit: yadi kim cana kartavyam ayam asmi praśādhi mām dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca
units.english: If there is anything to be done, here I am, command me!' "Dhritarashtra said, 'O Vidura, Sanjaya hath come back.

units.sanskrit: saṃjayaḥ vidura prāptaḥ garhayitvā ca mām gataḥ
units.english: He hath gone away after rebuking me.

units.sanskrit: ajātaśatroḥ śvas vākyam sabhā madhye sa vakṣyati
units.english: Tomorrow he will deliver, in the midst of the court, Ajatasatru's message.

units.sanskrit: tasya adya kuru vīrasya na vijñātam vacaḥ mayā
units.english: I have not been able today to ascertain what the message is of the Kuru hero.

units.sanskrit: tat me dahati gātrāṇi tat akārṣīt prajāgaram
units.english: Therefore, my body is burning, and that hath produced sleeplessness.

units.sanskrit: jāgrataḥ dahyamānasya śreyaḥ yat iha paśyasi
units.english: Tell us what may be good for a person that is sleepless and burning.

units.sanskrit: tat brūhi tvam hi naḥ tāta dharma artha kuśalaḥ hi asi
units.english: Thou art, O child, versed in both religion and profit.

units.sanskrit: yatas prāptaḥ saṃjayaḥ pāṇḍavebhyaḥ na me yathāvat manasaḥ praśāntiḥ
units.english: Ever since, Sanjaya hath returned from the Pandavas, my heart knoweth no peace.

units.sanskrit: sarva indriyāṇi aprakṛtim gatāni kim vakṣyati iti eva hi me adya cintā
units.english: Filled with anxiety about what he may deliver, all my senses have been disordered'.

units.sanskrit: viduraḥ uvāca abhiyuktam balavatā durbalam hīna sādhanam
units.english: "Vidura said, 'Sleeplessness overtaketh thief, a lustful person, him that hath lost all his wealth, him that hath failed to achieve success, and him also that is weak and hath been attacked by a strong person.

units.sanskrit: kaccit etaiḥ mahā doṣaiḥ na spṛṣṭaḥ asi narādhipa
units.english: I hope, O king, that none of these grave calamities have overtaken thee.

units.sanskrit: kaccit na para vitteṣu gṛdhyan viparitapyase dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca śrotum icchāmi te dharmyam param naiḥśreyasam vacaḥ
units.english: I hope, thou dost not grieve, coveting the wealth of others.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'I desire to hear from thee words that are beneficial and fraught with high morality.

units.sanskrit: asmin rājarṣi vaṃśe hi tvam ekaḥ prājña saṃmataḥ viduraḥ uvāca rājā lakṣaṇa saṃpannaḥ trailokyasya api yaḥ bhavet
units.english: In this race of royal Rishis thou alone art reverenced by the wise.' Vidura replied, 'King (Yudhishthira), graced with every virtue, is worthy of being the sovereign of the three worlds;

units.sanskrit: preṣyaḥ te preṣitaḥ ca eva dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
units.english: yet, O Dhritarashtra, however worthy of being kept by thy side, he was exiled by thee.

units.sanskrit: viparītataraḥ ca tvam bhāgadheyena saṃmataḥ
units.english: Thou art, however, possessed of qualities which are thy very reverse of those possessed by him.

units.sanskrit: arciṣā prajñayā ca eva dharma ātmā dharma kovidaḥ ānṛśaṃsyāt anukrośāt dharmāt satya parākramāt guru tvam tvayi saṃprekṣya bahūn kleśān titikṣate
units.english: In consequence of his inoffensiveness and kindness, his righteousness, love of truth and energy, and his remembering the reverence that is due to thee, Yudhishthira patiently bears innumerable wrongs.

units.sanskrit: duryodhane saubaleye karṇe duḥśāsane tathā eteṣu aiśvaryam ādhāya katham tvam bhūtim icchasi ātma jñānam samārambhaḥ titikṣā dharma nitya tā
units.english: Having bestowed on Duryodhana and Suvala's son and Karna, and Dussasana the management of the empire, how canst thou hope for prosperity? He that is not served from the high ends of life by the aid of self-knowledge, exertion, forbearance and steadiness in virtue, is called wise.

units.sanskrit: anāstikaḥ śraddadhānaḥ etat paṇḍita lakṣaṇam
units.english: These again are the marks of a wise man, viz., adherence to acts, worthy of praise and rejection of what is blamable, faith, and reverence.

units.sanskrit: krodhaḥ harṣaḥ ca darpaḥ ca hrī stambhaḥ mānya māni tā yam arthān na apakarṣanti sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He whom neither anger nor joy, nor pride, nor false modesty, nor stupefaction, nor vanity, can draw away from the high ends of life, is considered as wise.

units.sanskrit: yasya kṛtyam na jānanti mantram vā mantritam pare kṛtam eva asya jānanti sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He whose intended acts, and proposed counsels remain concealed from foes, and whose acts become known only after they have been done, is considered wise.

units.sanskrit: yasya kṛtyam na vighnanti śītam uṣṇam bhayam ratiḥ samṛddhiḥ asamṛddhiḥ vā sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He whose proposed actions are never obstructed by heat or cold, fear of attachment, prosperity or adversity, is considered wise.

units.sanskrit: yasya saṃsāriṇī prajñā dharma arthau anuvartate kāmāt artham vṛṇīte yaḥ sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He whose judgment dissociated from desire, followeth both virtue and profit, and who disregarding pleasure chooseth such ends as are serviceable in both worlds, is considered wise.

units.sanskrit: yathāśakti cikīrṣanti yathāśakti ca kurvate
units.english: They that exert to the best of their might, and act also to the best of their might, and disregard nothing as insignificant, are called wise.

units.sanskrit: kṣipram vijānāti ciram śṛṇoti vijñāya ca artham bhajate na kāmāt na a saṃpṛṣṭaḥ vyupayuṅkte para arthe
units.english: He that understandeth quickly, listeneth patiently, pursueth his objects with judgment and not from desire and spendeth not his breath on the affairs of others without being asked, is said to possess the foremost mark of wisdom.

units.sanskrit: na a prāpyam abhivāñchanti naṣṭam na icchanti śocitum āpatsu ca na muhyanti narāḥ paṇḍita buddhayaḥ
units.english: They that do not strive for objects that are unattainable, that do not grieve for what is lost and gone, that do not suffer their minds to be clouded amid calamities, are regarded to possess intellects endued with wisdom.

units.sanskrit: niścitya yaḥ prakramate na antar vasati karmaṇaḥ avandhya kālaḥ vaśya ātmā sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He who striveth, having commenced anything, till it is completed, who never wasteth his time, and who hath his soul under control, is regarded wise.

units.sanskrit: ārya karmaṇi rajyante bhūti karmāṇi kurvate hitam ca na abhyasūyanti paṇḍitāḥ bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: They that are wise, O bull of the Bharata race, always delight in honest deeds, do what tendeth to their happiness and prosperity, and never sneer at what is good.

units.sanskrit: na hṛṣyati ātma saṃmāne na avamānena tapyate gāṅgaḥ hradaḥ iva akṣobhyaḥ yaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: He who exulteth not at honours, and grieveth not at slights, and remaineth cool and unagitated like a lake in the course of Ganga, is reckoned as wise.

units.sanskrit: tattva jñaḥ sarva bhūtānām yoga jñaḥ sarva karmaṇām
units.english: That man who knoweth the nature of all creatures (viz., that everything is subject to destruction), who is cognisant also of the connections of all acts, and who is proficient in the knowledge of the means that men may resort to (for attaining their objects), is reckoned as wise.

units.sanskrit: upāya jñaḥ manuṣyāṇām naraḥ paṇḍitaḥ ucyate pravṛtta vāc citra kathaḥ ūhavān pratibhānavān
units.english: He who speaketh boldly, can converse on various subjects, knoweth the science of argumentation, possesseth genius, and can interpret the meaning of what is writ in books, is reckoned as wise.

units.sanskrit: āśu granthasya vaktā ca sa vai paṇḍitaḥ ucyate śrutam prajñā anugam yasya prajñā ca eva śruta anugā asaṃbhinna ārya maryādaḥ paṇḍita ākhyām labheta saḥ
units.english: He whose studies are regulated by reason, and whose reason followeth the scriptures, and who never abstaineth from paying respect to those that are good, is called a wise man.

units.sanskrit: aśrutaḥ ca samunnaddhaḥ daridraḥ ca mahāmanāḥ arthān ca akarmaṇā prepsuḥ mūḍhaḥ iti ucyate budhaiḥ
units.english: He, on the other hand, who is ignorant of scripture yet vain, poor yet proud, and who resorteth to unfair means for the acquisition of his objects, is a fool.

units.sanskrit: svam artham yaḥ parityajya para artham anutiṣṭhati mithyā carati mitra arthe yaḥ ca mūḍhaḥ saḥ ucyate
units.english: He who, forsaking his own, concerneth himself with the objects of others, and who practiseth deceitful means for serving his friends, is called a fool.

units.sanskrit: akāmān kāmayati yaḥ kāmayānān paridviṣan balavantam ca yaḥ dveṣṭi tam āhuḥ mūḍha cetasam
units.english: He who wisheth for those things that should not be desired, and forsaketh those that may legitimately be desired, and who beareth malice to those that are powerful, is regarded to be a foolish soul.

units.sanskrit: amitram kurute mitram mitram dveṣṭi hinasti ca karma ca ārabhate duṣṭam tam āhuḥ mūḍha cetasam
units.english: He who regardeth his foe as his friend, who hateth and beareth malice to his friend, and who committeth wicked deeds, is said to be a person of foolish soul.

units.sanskrit: saṃsārayati kṛtyāni sarvatra vicikitsate ciram karoti kṣipra arthe sa mūḍhaḥ bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: O bull of the Bharata race, he who divulgeth his projects, doubteth in all things, and spendeth a long time in doing what requireth a short time, is a fool.

units.sanskrit: śrāddham pitṛbhyaḥ na dadāti daivatāni na ca arcati suhṛd mitram na labhate tam āhuḥ mūḍha lakṣaṇam
units.english: He who doth not perform the Sraddha for the Pitris, nor worshippeth the deities, nor acquireth noble-minded friends, is said to be a person of foolish soul.

units.sanskrit: an āhūtaḥ praviśati a pṛṣṭaḥ bahu bhāṣate viśvasati apramatteṣu mūḍha cetāḥ nara adhamaḥ
units.english: That worst of men who entereth a place uninvited, and talketh much without being asked, and reposeth trust on untrustworthy wights, is a fool.

units.sanskrit: param kṣipati doṣeṇa vartamānaḥ svayam tathā yaḥ ca krudhyati anīśaḥ san sa ca mūḍhatamaḥ naraḥ
units.english: That man who being himself guilty casteth the blame on others, and who though impotent giveth vent to anger, is the most foolish of men.

units.sanskrit: ātmanaḥ balam a jñāya dharma artha parivarjitam alabhyam icchan naiṣkarmyāt mūḍha buddhiḥ iha ucyate
units.english: That man, who, without knowing his own strength and dissociated from both virtue and profit, desireth an object difficult of acquisition, without again adopting adequate means, is said to be destitute of intelligence.

units.sanskrit: a śiṣyam śāsti yaḥ rājan yaḥ ca śūnyam upāsate kadaryam bhajate yaḥ ca tam āhuḥ mūḍha cetasam
units.english: O king, he who punisheth one that is undeserving of punishment, payeth homage to persons without their knowledge, and waiteth upon misers, is said to be of little sense.

units.sanskrit: artham mahāntam āsādya vidyām aiśvaryam eva vā vicarati asamunnaddhaḥ yaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ ucyate
units.english: But he that, having attained immense wealth and prosperity or acquired (vast) learning, doth not bear himself haughtily, is reckoned as wise.

units.sanskrit: ekaḥ saṃpannam aśnāti vaḥ te vāsaḥ ca śobhanam yaḥ a saṃvibhajya bhṛtyebhyaḥ kaḥ nṛśaṃsataraḥ tatas ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalam bhuṅkte mahājanaḥ
units.english: Who, again, is more heartless than he, who, though possessed of affluence, eateth himself and weareth excellent robes himself without distributing his wealth among his dependents? While one person committeth sins, many reap the advantage resulting therefrom;

units.sanskrit: bhoktāraḥ vipramucyante kartā doṣeṇa lipyate
units.english: (yet in the end) it is the doer alone to whom the sin attacheth while those that enjoy the fruit escape unhurt.

units.sanskrit: ekam hanyāt na vā hanyāt iṣuḥ muktaḥ dhanuṣmatā
units.english: When a bowman shooteth an arrow, he may or may not succeed in slaying even a single person, but when an intelligent individual applieth his intelligence (viciously);

units.sanskrit: buddhiḥ buddhimatā utsṛṣṭā hanyāt rāṣṭram sa rājakam
units.english: it may destroy an entire kingdom with the king.

units.sanskrit: ekayā dve viniścitya trīn caturbhiḥ vaśe kuru pañca jitvā viditvā ṣaṭ sapta hitvā sukhī bhava
units.english: Discriminating the two by means of the one, bring under thy subjection the three by means of four, and also conquering the five and knowing the six, and abstaining from the seven, be happy.

units.sanskrit: ekam viṣa rasaḥ hanti śastreṇa ekaḥ ca vadhyate
units.english: Poison slayeth but one person, and a weapon also but one;

units.sanskrit: sa rāṣṭram sa prajam hanti rājānam mantra visravaḥ
units.english: wicked counsels, however, destroy an entire kingdom with king and subject.

units.sanskrit: ekaḥ svādu na bhuñjīta ekaḥ ca arthān na cintayet ekaḥ na gacchet adhvānam na ekaḥ supteṣu jāgṛyāt
units.english: Alone one should not partake of any savoury viand, nor alone reflect on concerns of profit, nor alone go upon a journey, nor alone remain awake among sleeping companions.

units.sanskrit: ekam eva advitīyam tat yat rājan na avabudhyase satyam svargasya sopānam pārāvārasya nauḥ iva
units.english: That Being who is One without a second, and whom, O king, thou hast not been able to comprehend, is Truth's self, and the Way to heaven, even like a boat in the ocean.

units.sanskrit: ekaḥ kṣamāvatām doṣaḥ dvitīyaḥ na upalabhyate
units.english: There is one only defect in forgiving persons, and not another;

units.sanskrit: yat enam kṣamayā yuktam aśaktam manyate janaḥ
units.english: that defect is that people take a forgiving person to be weak.

units.sanskrit: saḥ asya doṣaḥ na mantavyaḥ kṣamā hi paramam balam
units.english: That defect, however, should not be taken into consideration, for forgiveness is a great power.

units.sanskrit: kṣamā guṇaḥ hi aśaktānām śaktānām bhūṣaṇam kṣamā
units.english: Forgiveness is a virtue of the weak, and an ornament of the strong.

units.sanskrit: kṣamā vaśīkṛtiḥ loke kṣamayā kim na sādhyate
units.english: Forgiveness subdueth (all) in this world;

units.sanskrit: śānti khaḍgaḥ kare yasya kim kariṣyati durjanaḥ a tṛṇe patitaḥ vahniḥ svayam eva upaśāmyati
units.english: what is there that forgiveness cannot achieve? What can a wicked person do unto him who carrieth the sabre of forgiveness in his hand? Fire falling on a grassless ground is extinguished of itself.

units.sanskrit: akṣamāvān param doṣaiḥ ātmānam ca eva yojayet
units.english: And unforgiving individual defileth himself with many enormities.

units.sanskrit: ekaḥ dharmaḥ param śreyaḥ kṣamā ekā śāntiḥ uttamā
units.english: Righteousness is the one highest good; and forgiveness is the one supreme peace;

units.sanskrit: vidyā ekā paramā dṛṣṭiḥ ahiṃsā ekā sukha āvahā
units.english: knowledge is one supreme contentment; and benevolence, one sole happiness.

units.sanskrit: dvau imau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpaḥ bila śayān iva rājānam ca aviroddhāram brāhmaṇam ca a pravāsinam
units.english: Even as a serpent devoureth animals living in holes, the earth devoureth these two, viz., a king who is incompetent to fight, and a Brahmana who doth not sojourn to holy places.

units.sanskrit: dve karmaṇī naraḥ kurvan asmin loke virocate abruvan paruṣam kim cit asataḥ na arthayan tathā
units.english: A man may attain renown in this world by doing two things, viz., by refraining from harsh speech, and by disregarding those that are wicked.

units.sanskrit: dvau imau puruṣa vyāghra para pratyaya kāriṇau striyaḥ kāmita kāminyaḥ lokaḥ pūjita pūjakaḥ
units.english: O tiger among men, these two have not a will of their own, viz., those women who covet men simply because the latter are coveted by others of their sex, and that person who worships another simply because the latter is worshipped by others.

units.sanskrit: dvau imau kaṇṭakau tīkṣṇau śarīra pariśoṣaṇau
units.english: These two are like sharp thorns afflicting the body, viz., the desires of a poor man, and the anger of the impotent.

units.sanskrit: dvau imau na virājete viparītena karmaṇā gṛhasthaḥ ca nirārambhaḥ kāryavān ca eva bhikṣukaḥ
units.english: These two persons never shine because of their incompatible acts, viz., a householder without exertion, and a beggar busied in schemes.

units.sanskrit: dvau imau puruṣau rājan svargasya upari tiṣṭhataḥ prabhuḥ ca kṣamayā yuktaḥ daridraḥ ca pradānavān
units.english: These two, O king, live (as it were) in a region higher than heaven itself, viz., a man of power endued with forgiveness, and poor man that is charitable.

units.sanskrit: nyāya āgatasya dravyasya boddhavyau dvau atikramau
units.english: Of things honestly got, these two must be looked upon as misuse, viz., making gifts to the unworthy and refusing the worthy.

units.sanskrit: a pātre pratipattiḥ ca pātre ca a pratipādanam dvau ambhasi niveṣṭavyau gale baddhvā dṛḍhām śilām dhanavantam a dātāram daridram ca a tapasvinam
units.english: These two should be thrown into the water, tightly binding weights to their necks, viz., a wealthy man that doth not give away, and a poor man that is proud.

units.sanskrit: trayaḥ nyāyāḥ manuṣyāṇām śrūyante bharata ṛṣabha kanīyān madhyamaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ iti veda vidaḥ viduḥ
units.english: O bull of the Bharata race, persons versed in the Vedas have said that men's means are good, middling, and bad.

units.sanskrit: trividhāḥ puruṣāḥ rājan uttama adhama madhyamāḥ
units.english: Men also, O king, are good, indifferent, and bad.

units.sanskrit: niyojayet yathāvat tān trividheṣu eva karmasu
units.english: They should, therefore, be respectively employed in that kind of work for which they may be fit.

units.sanskrit: trayaḥ eva adhanāḥ rājan bhāryā dāsaḥ tathā sutaḥ yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tat dhanam
units.english: These three, O king, cannot have wealth of their own, viz., the wife, the slave, and the son, and whatever may be earned by them would be his to whom they belong.

units.sanskrit: haraṇam ca para svānām para dāra abhimarśanam suhṛdaḥ ca parityāgaḥ trayaḥ doṣāḥ kṣaya āvahāḥ
units.english: Great fear springeth from these three crimes, viz., theft of other's property, outrage on other's wives, and breach with friend.

units.sanskrit: trividham narakasya idam dvāram nāśanam ātmanaḥ kāmaḥ krodhaḥ tathā lobhaḥ tasmāt etat trayam tyajet
units.english: These three, besides, being destructive to one's own self, are the gates of hell, viz., lust, anger, and covetousness. Therefore, every one should renounce them.

units.sanskrit: bhaktam ca bhajamānam ca tava asmi iti ca vādinam trīn etān śaraṇam prāptān viṣame api na saṃtyajet
units.english: These three should never be forsaken even in imminent danger, viz., a follower, one who seeks protection, saying,--I am thine,--and lastly one who hath come to your abode.

units.sanskrit: vara pradānam rājyam ca putra janma ca bhārata śatroḥ ca mokṣaṇam kṛcchrāt trīṇi ca ekam ca tad samam
units.english: Verily, O Bharata, liberating a foe from distress, alone amounteth in point of merit, to these three taken together, viz., conferring a boon, acquiring a kingdom, and obtaining a son.

units.sanskrit: catvāri rājñā tu mahā balena varjyāni āhuḥ paṇḍitaḥ tāni vidyāt alpa prajñaiḥ saha mantram na kuryān
units.english: Learned men have declared that a king, although powerful, should never consult with these four, viz., men of small sense, men that are procrastinating, men that are indolent, and men that are flatterers.

units.sanskrit: catvāri te tāta gṛhe vasantu śriyā abhijuṣṭasya gṛhastha dharme vṛddhaḥ jñātiḥ avasannaḥ kulīnaḥ
units.english: O sire, crowned with prosperity and leading the life of a householder, let these four dwell with thee, viz., old consanguineous, relatives, high-born persons fallen into adversity, poor friends, and issueless sisters.

units.sanskrit: catvāri āha mahā rāja sadyaskāni bṛhaspatiḥ pṛcchate tridaśa indrāya tāni imāni nibodha me devatānām ca saṃkalpam anubhāvam ca dhīmatām
units.english: On being asked by the chief of the celestials, Vrihaspati, O mighty king declared four things capable of fructifying or occurring within a single day, viz., the resolve of the gods, the comprehensions of intelligent persons, the humility of learned men, and the destruction of the sinful.

units.sanskrit: catvāri karmāṇi abhayaṃkarāṇi bhayam prayacchanti a yathā kṛtāni māna agnihotram uta māna maunam
units.english: These four that are calculated to remove fear, bring on fear when they are improperly performed, viz., the Agni-hotra, the vow of silence, study, and sacrifice (in general).

units.sanskrit: mānena adhītam uta māna yajñaḥ pañca agnayaḥ manuṣyeṇa paricaryāḥ prayatnataḥ pitā mātā agniḥ ātmā ca guruḥ ca bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: O bull of the Bharata race, these five fires, should be worshipped with regard by a person, viz., father, mother, fire (proper), soul and preceptor.

units.sanskrit: pañca eva pūjayan loke yaśaḥ prāpnoti kevalam devān pitṝn manuṣyān ca bhikṣūn atithi pañcamān
units.english: By serving these five, men attain great fame in this world, viz., the gods, the Pitris, men, beggars, and guests.

units.sanskrit: pañca tvā anugamiṣyanti yatra yatra gamiṣyasi mitrāṇi amitrāḥ madhyasthāḥ upajīvya upajīvinaḥ
units.english: These five follow thee wherever thou goest, viz., friends, foes, those that are indifferent, dependants, and those that are entitled to maintenance.

units.sanskrit: pañca indriyasya martyasya chidram ced ekam indriyam tatas asya sravati prajñā dṛteḥ pādāt iva udakam
units.english: Of the five senses beholding to man, if one springeth a leak, then from that single hole runneth out all his intelligence, even like water running out from a perforated leathern vessel.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ doṣāḥ puruṣeṇa iha hātavyāḥ bhūtim icchatā nidrā tandrī bhayam krodhaḥ ālasyam dīrghasūtra tā
units.english: The six faults should be avoided by a person who wisheth to attain prosperity, viz., sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, indolence and procrastination.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ imān puruṣaḥ jahyāt bhinnām nāvam iva arṇave a pravaktāram ācāryam an adhīyānam ṛtvijam a rakṣitāram rājānam bhāryām ca a priya vādinīm
units.english: These six should be renounced like a splitting vessel in the sea, viz., a preceptor that cannot expound the scriptures, a priest that is illiterate, a king that is unable to protect, a wife that speaketh disagreeable words, a cow-herd that doth not wish to go to the fields, and a barber that wisheth to renounce a village for the woods.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ eva tu guṇāḥ puṃsā na hātavyāḥ kadā cana satyam dānam anālasyam anasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ
units.english: Verily, those six qualities should never be forsaken by men, viz., truth, charity, diligence, benevolence, forgiveness and patience.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ imāni vinaśyanti muhūrtam an avekṣaṇāt gāvaḥ sevā kṛṣiḥ bhāryā vidyā vṛṣala saṃgatiḥ
units.english: These six are instantly destroyed, if neglected, viz., kine, service, agriculture, a wife, learning, and the wealth of a Sudra.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ ete hi avamanyante nityam pūrva upakāriṇam ācāryam śikṣitāḥ śiṣyāḥ kṛta dārāḥ ca mātaram
units.english: These six forget those who have bestowed obligations on them, viz., educated disciples, their preceptors; married persons, their mothers;

units.sanskrit: nārīm vigata kāmāḥ tu kṛtārthāḥ ca prayojanam
units.english: persons whose desires have been gratified, women; they who have achieved success, they who had rendered aid;

units.sanskrit: nāvam nistīrṇa kāntārāḥ āturāḥ ca cikitsakam
units.english: and patients that have been cured, their physicians.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ jīva lokasya sukhāni rājan
units.english: Health, unindebtedness, living at home, companionship with good men, certainty as regards the means of livelihood, and living without fear, these six. O king, conduce to the happiness of men.

units.sanskrit: īrṣuḥ ghṛṇī na saṃtuṣṭaḥ krodhanaḥ nitya śaṅkitaḥ para bhāgya upajīvī ca ṣaṭ ete nitya duḥkhitāḥ artha āgamaḥ nityam arogi tā ca
units.english: These six are always miserable, viz., the envious, the malicious, the discontented, the irascible, the ever-suspicious, and those depending upon the fortunes of others.

units.sanskrit: priyā ca bhāryā priya vādinī ca vaśyaḥ ca putraḥ artha karī ca vidyā ṣaṭ jīva lokasya sukhāni rājan
units.english: These six, O king, comprise the happiness of men, viz., acquirement of wealth, uninterrupted health, a beloved and a sweet-speeched wife, an obedient son, and knowledge that is lucrative.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṇṇām ātmani nityānām aiśvaryam yaḥ adhigacchati na sa pāpaiḥ kutas anarthaiḥ yujyate vijita indriyaḥ
units.english: He that succeedeth in gaining the mastery over the six that are always present in the human heart, being thus the master of his senses, never committeth sin, and therefore suffereth calamity.

units.sanskrit: ṣaṭ ime ṣaṭsu jīvanti saptamaḥ na upalabhyate
units.english: These six may be seen to subsist upon other six, viz., thieves, upon persons that are careless;

units.sanskrit: corāḥ pramatte jīvanti vyādhiteṣu cikitsakāḥ
units.english: physicians, on persons that are ailing;

units.sanskrit: pramadāḥ kāmayāneṣu yajamāneṣu yājakāḥ
units.english: women, upon persons suffering from lust; priests, upon them that sacrifice;

units.sanskrit: rājā vivadamāneṣu nityam mūrkheṣu paṇḍitāḥ
units.english: a king, upon persons that quarrel; and lastly men of learning, upon them that are without it.

units.sanskrit: sapta doṣāḥ sadā rājñā hātavyāḥ vyasana udayāḥ prāyaśas yaiḥ vinaśyanti kṛta mūlāḥ ca pārthivāḥ
units.english: A king should renounce these seven faults that are productive of calamity, inasmuch as they are able to effect the ruin of even monarchs firmly established;

units.sanskrit: striyaḥ akṣāḥ mṛgayā pānam vāc pāruṣyam ca pañcamam mahat ca daṇḍa pāruṣyam artha dūṣaṇam eva ca
units.english: these are women, dice, hunting, drinking, harshness of speech, severity of punishment, and misuse of wealth.

units.sanskrit: aṣṭau pūrva nimittāni narasya vinaśiṣyataḥ brāhmaṇān prathamam dveṣṭi brāhmaṇaiḥ ca virudhyate
units.english: These eight are the immediate indications of a man destined to destruction, viz., hating the Brahmanas, disputes with Brahmanas, appropriation of a Brahmana's possessions, taking the life of Brahmana, taking a pleasure in reviling Brahmanas, grieving to hear the praises of Brahmanas, forgetting them on ceremonious occasions, and giving vent to spite when they ask for anything.

units.sanskrit: etān doṣān naraḥ prājñaḥ buddhyā buddhvā vivarjayet
units.english: These transgressions a wise man should understand, and understanding, eschew.

units.sanskrit: aṣṭau imāni harṣasya navanītāni bhārata vartamānāni dṛśyante tāni eva su sukhāni api samāgamaḥ ca sakhibhiḥ mahān ca eva dhana āgamaḥ
units.english: These eight, O Bharata, are the very cream of happiness, and these only are attainable here, viz., meeting with friends, accession of immense wealth, embracing a son, union for intercourse, conversation with friends in proper times, the advancement of persons belong to one's own party, the acquisition of what had been anticipated, and respect in society.

units.sanskrit: abhipretasya lābhaḥ ca pūjā ca jana saṃsadi
units.english: These eight qualities glorify a man, viz., wisdom, high birth, self-restraint, learning, prowess, moderation in speech gift according to one's power, and gratitude.

units.sanskrit: nava dvāram idam veśma tri sthūṇam pañca sākṣikam
units.english: This house hath nine doors, three pillars, and five witnesses. It is presided over by the soul.

units.sanskrit: kṣetrajña adhiṣṭhitam vidvān yaḥ veda sa paraḥ kaviḥ
units.english: That learned man who knoweth all this is truly wise.

units.sanskrit: daśa dharmam na jānanti dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha tān mattaḥ pramattaḥ unmattaḥ śrāntaḥ kruddhaḥ bubhukṣitaḥ tvaramāṇaḥ ca bhīruḥ ca lubdhaḥ kāmī ca te daśa
units.english: O Dhritarashtra, these ten do not know what virtue is viz., the intoxicated, inattentive, the raving, the fatigued, the angry, the starving, the hasty, the covetous, the frightened, and the lustful.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt eteṣu bhāveṣu na prasajjeta paṇḍitaḥ
units.english: Therefore, he that is wise must eschew the company of these.

units.sanskrit: atra eva udāharanti imam itihāsam purātanam putra artham asura indreṇa gītam ca eva sudhanvanā
units.english: In this connection is cited the old story about what transpired between Suyodhana and (Prahlada), the chief of the Asuras in relation to the latter's son.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ kāma manyū prajahāti rājā pātre pratiṣṭhāpayate dhanam ca viśeṣa vid śrutavān kṣiprakārī
units.english: That king who renounceth lust and anger, who bestoweth wealth upon proper recipients, and is discriminating, learned, and active, is regarded as an authority of all men.

units.sanskrit: vijñāta doṣeṣu dadhāti daṇḍam jānāti mātrām ca tathā kṣamām ca tam tādṛśam śrīḥ juṣate samagrā
units.english: Great prosperity attends upon that king who knoweth how to inspire confidence in others, who inflicteth punishment on those whose guilt hath been proved, who is acquainted with the proper measure of punishment, and who knoweth when mercy is to be shown.

units.sanskrit: su durbalam na avajānāti kam cit
units.english: He is a wise person who doth not disregard even a weak foe;

units.sanskrit: yuktaḥ ripum sevate buddhi pūrvam
units.english: who proceeds with intelligence in respect of a foe, anxiously watching for an opportunity;

units.sanskrit: na vigraham rocayate balasthaiḥ
units.english: who doth not desire hostilities with persons stronger than himself;

units.sanskrit: kāle ca yaḥ vikramate sa dhīraḥ
units.english: and who displayeth his prowess in season.

units.sanskrit: udyogam anvicchati ca apramattaḥ duḥkham ca kāle sahate jita ātmā dhuraṃdharaḥ tasya jitāḥ sapatnāḥ
units.english: That illustrious person who doth not grieve when a calamity hath already come upon him, who exerteth with all his senses collected, and who patiently beareth misery in season, is certainly the foremost of persons, and all his foes are vanquished.

units.sanskrit: pāpaiḥ saṃdhim para dāra abhimarśam dambham stainyam paiśunam madya pānam na sevate yaḥ sa sukhī sadā eva
units.english: He who doth not live away from hope uselessly, who doth not make friends with sinful persons, who never outrageth another's wife, who never betrayeth arrogance, and who never committeth a theft or showeth ingratitude or indulgeth in drinking is always happy.

units.sanskrit: na a pūjitaḥ kupyati ca api a mūḍhaḥ
units.english: He who never boastfully striveth to attain the three objects of human pursuit, who when asked, telleth the truth, who quarreleth not even for the sake of friends, and who never becometh angry though slighted, is reckoned as wise.

units.sanskrit: na ati āha kim cit kṣamate vivādam sarvatra tādṛś labhate praśaṃsām yaḥ na uddhatam kurute jātu veṣam
units.english: He who beareth not malice towards others but is kind to all, who being weak disputeth not with others, who speaketh not arrogantly, and forgeteth a quarrel, is praised everywhere.

units.sanskrit: na pauruṣeṇa api vikatthate anyān na mūrchitaḥ kaṭukāni āha kim cit priyam sadā tam kurute janaḥ api
units.english: That man who never assumeth a haughty mien, who never censureth others praising himself the while, and never addresseth harsh words to others for getting himself, is ever loved by all.

units.sanskrit: na darpam ārohati na astam eti na durgataḥ asmi iti karoti manyum tam ārya śīlam param āhuḥ agryam
units.english: He who raketh not up old hostilities, who behaveth neither arrogantly nor with too much humility, and who even when distressed never committeth an improper act, is considered by respectable men a person of good conduct.

units.sanskrit: na sve sukhe vai kurute praharṣam na anyasya duḥkhe bhavati pratītaḥ dattvā na paścāt kurute anutāpam
units.english: He who exulteth not at his own happiness, nor delighteth in another's misery, and who repenteth not after having made a gift, is said to be a man of good nature and conduct.

units.sanskrit: deśa ācārān samayān jāti dharmān bubhūṣate yaḥ tu parāvara jñaḥ
units.english: He who desireth to obtain a knowledge of the customs of different countries, and also the languages of different nations, and of the usages of different orders of men, knoweth at once all that is high and low;

units.sanskrit: sa tatra tatra adhigataḥ sadā eva
units.english: and wherever he may go, he is sure to gain an ascendancy over even those that are glad.

units.sanskrit: rāja dviṣṭam paiśunam pūga vairam matta unmattaiḥ durjanaiḥ ca api vādam yaḥ prajñāvān varjayet sa pradhānaḥ
units.english: The intelligent man who relinquisheth pride, folly, insolence, sinful acts, disloyalty towards the king, crookedness of behaviour, enmity with many, and also quarrels with men that are drunk, mad and wicked, is the foremost of his species.

units.sanskrit: damam śaucam daivatam maṅgalāni prāyaścittam vividhān lokavādān etāni yaḥ kurute naityakāni
units.english: The very gods bestow prosperity upon him who daily practiseth self-restraint, purification, auspicious rites, worship of the gods, expiatory ceremonies, and other rites of universal observance.

units.sanskrit: samaiḥ sakhyam vyavahāram kathāḥ ca guṇaiḥ viśiṣṭān ca purodadhāti vipaścitaḥ tasya nayāḥ su nītāḥ
units.english: The acts of that learned man are well-conceived, and well-applied who formeth matrimonial alliances with persons of equal positions and not with those that are inferior, who placeth those before him that are more qualified, and who talketh, behaveth and maketh friendships with persons of equal position.

units.sanskrit: mitam bhuṅkte saṃvibhajya āśritebhyaḥ mitam svapiti amitam karma kṛtvā dadāti amitreṣu api yācitaḥ san
units.english: He who eateth frugally after dividing the food amongst his dependants, who sleepeth little after working much, and who, when solicited giveth away even unto his foes, hath his soul under control, and calamities always keep themselves aloof from him.

units.sanskrit: cikīrṣitam viprakṛtam ca yasya na anye janāḥ karma jānanti kim cit mantre gupte samyak anuṣṭhite ca
units.english: He whose counsels are well-kept and well-carried out into practice, and whose acts in consequence thereof are never known by others to injure men, succeedeth in securing even his most trifling objects.

units.sanskrit: satyaḥ mṛduḥ dāna kṛt śuddha bhāvaḥ atīva saṃjñāyate jñāti madhye mahā maṇiḥ jātyaḥ iva prasannaḥ
units.english: He who is intent upon abstaining from injury to all creatures, who is truthful, gentle, charitable, and pure in mind, shineth greatly among his kinsmen like a precious gem of the purest ray having its origin in an excellent mine.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ātmanā apatrapate bhṛśam naraḥ sa sarva lokasya guruḥ bhavati uta
units.english: That man who feeleth shame even though his faults be not known to any save himself, is highly honoured among all men.

units.sanskrit: ananta tejāḥ sumanāḥ samāhitaḥ sva tejasā sūryaḥ iva avabhāsate
units.english: Possessed of a pure heart and boundless energy and abstracted within himself, he shineth in consequence of his energy like the very sun.

units.sanskrit: vane jātāḥ śāpa dagdhasya rājñaḥ pāṇḍoḥ putrāḥ pañca pañca indra kalpāḥ
units.english: King Pandu consumed by a (Brahmana's) curse, had five sons born unto him in the woods that are like five Indras.

units.sanskrit: tvayā eva bālāḥ vardhitāḥ śikṣitāḥ ca
units.english: O son of Ambika, thou hast brought up those children and taught them everything.

units.sanskrit: tava ādeśam pālayanti āmbikeya
units.english: They are obedient to thy commands.

units.sanskrit: pradāya eṣām ucitam tāta rājyam sukhī putraiḥ sahitaḥ modamānaḥ
units.english: Giving them back their just share of the kingdom, O sire, filled with joy, be thou happy with thy sons.

units.sanskrit: na devānām na api ca mānuṣāṇām bhaviṣyasi tvam tarkaṇīyaḥ narendra dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca
units.english: Then, O monarch, thou shalt inspire confidence in both the gods and men.'" SECTION XXXIV "Dhritarashtra said, 'Tell me what may be done by a person that is sleepless and burning with anxieties, for thou alone amongst us, O child, art versed in both religion and profit.

units.sanskrit: tvam mām yathāvat vidura praśādhi
units.english: Advise me wisely, O Vidura.

units.sanskrit: śreyaskaram brūhi tat vai kurūṇām
units.english: O thou of magnanimous heart, tell me what is thou deemest to be beneficial for Ajatasatru and what is productive of good to the Kurus.

units.sanskrit: pāpa āśaṅkī pāpam eva anupaśyan
units.english: Apprehending future evils.

units.sanskrit: kave tat me brūhi sarvam yathāvan manīṣitam sarvam ajātaśatroḥ viduraḥ uvāca
units.english: I look back only on my previous guilt: I ask thee with anxious heart, O learned one, tell me what is exactly in Ajatasatru's mind,' "Vidura said, 'Even if unasked, one should speak truly, whether his words be good or bad, hateful or pleasing, unto him whose defeat one doth not wish.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt vakṣyāmi te rājan bhavam icchan kurūn prati
units.english: I shall, therefore, say, O king, what is for the good of the Kurus.

units.sanskrit: vacaḥ śreyaskaram dharmyam bruvataḥ tat nibodha me
units.english: Listen to me.

units.sanskrit: mithyā upetāni karmāṇi sidhyeyuḥ yāni bhārata anupāya prayuktāni mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ
units.english: Do not, O Bharata, set the heart upon means of success that are unjust and improper.

units.sanskrit: upāya yuktam medhāvī na tatra glapayet manaḥ
units.english: A man of intelligence must not grieve if any purpose of his doth not succeed, notwithstanding the application of fair and proper means.

units.sanskrit: anubandhān avekṣeta sa anubandheṣu karmasu
units.english: Before one engageth in an act, one should consider the competence of the agent, the nature of the act itself, and its purpose, for all acts are dependent on these.

units.sanskrit: saṃpradhārya ca kurvīta na vegena samācaret
units.english: Considering these one should begin an act, and not take it up on a sudden impulse.

units.sanskrit: anubandham ca saṃprekṣya vipākān ca eva karmaṇām utthānam ātmanaḥ ca eva dhīraḥ kurvīta vā na vā
units.english: He that is wise should either do an act or desist from it fully considering his own ability, the nature of the act, and the consequence also of success.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ pramāṇam na jānāti sthāne vṛddhau tathā kṣaye kośe janapade daṇḍe na sa rājye avatiṣṭhate
units.english: The king who knoweth not proportion or measure as regards territory, gain, loss, treasury, population, and punishment, cannot retain his kingdom long.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ tu etāni pramāṇāni yathā uktāni anupaśyati yuktaḥ dharma arthayoḥ jñāne sa rājyam adhigacchati
units.english: He, on the other hand, who is acquainted with the measures of these as prescribed in treatises, being necessarily possessed of the knowledge of religion and profit, can retain his kingdom.

units.sanskrit: indriyaiḥ indriya artheṣu vartamānaiḥ anigrahaiḥ taiḥ ayam tāpyate lokaḥ nakṣatrāṇi grahaiḥ iva
units.english: As the stars are affected by the planets, so is this world affected by the senses, when they are directed, uncontrolled, to their respective objects.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ jitaḥ pañcavargeṇa sahajena ātma karśinā āpadaḥ tasya vardhante śukla pakṣaḥ iva uḍurāj
units.english: Like the moon during the lighted fortnight, calamities increase in respect of him who is vanquished by the five senses in their natural state, which ever lead him towards various acts.

units.sanskrit: a vijitya yaḥ ātmānam amātyān vijigīṣate amitrān vā ajita amātyaḥ saḥ avaśaḥ parihīyate
units.english: He who wisheth to control his counsellors before controlling his own self, or to subdue his adversaries before controlling his counsellors, at last succumbs deprived of strength.

units.sanskrit: ātmānam eva prathamam deśa rūpeṇa yaḥ jayet tatas amātyān amitrān ca na mogham vijigīṣate
units.english: He, therefore, who first subdueth his own self regarding it as a foe, never faileth to subdue his counsellors and adversaries at last.

units.sanskrit: vaśya indriyam jita amātyam dhṛta daṇḍam vikāriṣu parīkṣya kāriṇam dhīram atyantam śrīḥ niṣevate
units.english: Great prosperity waiteth upon him who hath subdued his senses, or controlled his soul, or who is capable of punishing all offenders, or who acteth with judgment or who is blessed with patience.

units.sanskrit: rathaḥ śarīram puruṣasya rājan
units.english: One's body, O king, is one's car;

units.sanskrit: na ātmā niyantā indriyāṇi asya ca aśvāḥ
units.english: the soul within is the driver; and the senses are its steeds.

units.sanskrit: taiḥ apramattaḥ kuśalaḥ sat aśvaiḥ dāntaiḥ sukham yāti rathī iva dhīraḥ
units.english: Drawn by those excellent steeds, when well-trained, he that is wise, pleasantly performeth the journey of life, and awake in peace.

units.sanskrit: avidheyāḥ iva adāntāḥ hayāḥ pathi kusārathim
units.english: The horses that are unbroken and incapable of being controlled, always lead an unskilful driver to destruction in the course of the journey;

units.sanskrit: anartham arthataḥ paśyan artham ca eva api anarthataḥ indriyaiḥ prasṛtaḥ bālaḥ su duḥkham manyate sukham
units.english: The inexperienced wight, who, led by this unsubdued senses, hopeth to extract evil from good and good from evil, necessarily confoundeth misery with happiness.

units.sanskrit: dharma arthau yaḥ parityajya syāt indriya vaśa anugaḥ śrī prāṇa dhana dārebhya kṣipram sa parihīyate
units.english: He, who, forsaking religion and profit, followeth the lead of his senses, loseth without delay prosperity, life, wealth and wife.

units.sanskrit: arthānām īśvaraḥ yaḥ syāt indriyāṇām anīśvaraḥ indriyāṇām anaiśvaryāt aiśvaryāt bhraśyate hi saḥ
units.english: He, who is the master of riches but not of his senses, certainly loseth his riches in consequence of his want of mastery over his senses.

units.sanskrit: ātmanā ātmānam anvicchet manaḥ buddhīndriyaiḥ yataiḥ ātmā eva hi ātmanaḥ bandhuḥ ātmā eva ripuḥ ātmanaḥ
units.english: One should seek to know one's self by means of one's own self, controlling one's mind, intellect, and senses, for one's self is one's friend as, indeed, it is one's own foe.

units.sanskrit: bandhuḥ ātmā ātmanaḥ tasya yena eva ātmā ātmanā jitaḥ saḥ eva niyataḥ bandhuḥ saḥ eva niyataḥ ripuḥ
units.english: That man, who hath conquered self by means of self, hath his self for a friend, for one's self is ever one's friend or foe.

units.sanskrit: kṣudra akṣeṇa iva jālena jhaṣau apihitau ubhau kāmaḥ ca rājan krodhaḥ ca tau prajñānam vilumpataḥ
units.english: Desire and anger, O king, break through wisdom, just as a large fish breaks through a net of thin cords.

units.sanskrit: samavekṣya iha dharma arthau saṃbhārān yaḥ adhigacchati sa vai saṃbhṛta saṃbhāraḥ satatam sukham edhate
units.english: He, who in this world regarding both religion and profit, seeketh to acquire the means of success, winneth happiness, possessing all he had sought.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ pañca abhyantarān śatrūn a vijitya mati kṣayān jigīṣati ripūn anyān ripavaḥ abhibhavanti tam
units.english: He, who, without subduing his five inner foes of mental origin, wisheth to vanquish other adversaries, is, in fact, overpowered by the latter.

units.sanskrit: dṛśyante hi durātmānaḥ vadhyamānāḥ sva karmabhiḥ indriyāṇām anīśa tvāt rājānaḥ rājya vibhramaiḥ
units.english: It is seen that many evil-minded kings, owing to want of mastery over their senses, are ruined by acts of their own, occasioned by the lust of territory.

units.sanskrit: a saṃtyāgāt pāpa kṛtām a pāpān tulyaḥ daṇḍaḥ spṛśate miśra bhāvāt śuṣkeṇa ārdram dahyate miśra bhāvāt
units.english: As fuel that is wet burneth with that which is dry, so a sinless man is punished equally with the sinful in consequence of constant association with the latter.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt pāpaiḥ saha saṃdhim na kuryāt
units.english: Therefore, friendship with the sinful should be avoided.

units.sanskrit: nijān utpatataḥ śatrūn pañca pañca prayojanān yaḥ mohāt na nigṛhṇāti tam āpad grasate naram
units.english: He that, from ignorance, faileth to control his five greedy foes, having five distinct objects, is overwhelmed by calamities.

units.sanskrit: anasūyā ārjavam śaucam saṃtoṣaḥ priya vādi tā damaḥ satyam anāyāsaḥ na bhavanti durātmanām
units.english: Guilelessness and simplicity, purity and contentment, sweetness of speech and self-restraint, truth and steadiness,--these are never the attributes of the wicked.

units.sanskrit: ātma jñānam anāyāsaḥ titikṣā dharma nitya tā vāc ca eva guptā dānam ca na etāni antyeṣu bhārata
units.english: Self-knowledge and steadiness, patience and devotion to virtue, competence to keep counsels and charity,--these,--O Bharata, never exist in inferior men.

units.sanskrit: ākrośa parivādābhyām vihiṃsanti abudhāḥ budhān vaktā pāpam upādatte kṣamamāṇaḥ vimucyate
units.english: Fools seek to injure the wise by false reproaches and evil speeches, The consequence is, that by this they take upon themselves the sins of the wise, while the latter, freed from their sins, are forgiven.

units.sanskrit: hiṃsā balam asādhūnām rājñām daṇḍa vidhiḥ balam śuśrūṣā tu balam strīṇām kṣamā guṇavatām balam
units.english: in criminal code, the strength of kings, in attentions of the weak and of women;

units.sanskrit: vāc saṃyamaḥ hi nṛpate su duṣkaratamaḥ mataḥ
units.english: and in forgiveness that of the virtuous. To control speech, O king, is said to be most difficult.

units.sanskrit: arthavat ca vicitram ca na śakyam bahu bhāṣitum
units.english: It is not easy to hold a long conversation uttering words full of meaning and delightful to the hearers.

units.sanskrit: abhyāvahati kalyāṇam vividhā vāc su bhāṣitā
units.english: Well-spoken speech is productive of many beneficial results;

units.sanskrit: sā eva durbhāṣitā rājan anarthāya upapadyate
units.english: and ill-spoken speech, O king, is the cause of evils.

units.sanskrit: saṃrohati śaraiḥ viddham vanam paraśunā hatam vācā duruktam bībhatsam na saṃrohati vāc kṣatam
units.english: A forest pierced by arrows, or cut down by hatchets may again grow, but one's heart wounded and censured by ill-spoken words never recovereth.

units.sanskrit: karṇi nālīka nārācāḥ nirharanti śarīrataḥ vāc śalyaḥ tu na nirhartum śakyaḥ hṛdiśayaḥ hi saḥ
units.english: Weapons, such as arrows, bullets, and bearded darts, can be easily extracted from the body, but a wordy dagger plunged deep into the heart is incapable of being taken out.

units.sanskrit: vāc sāyakāḥ vadanāt niṣpatanti
units.english: Wordy arrows are shot from the mouth;

units.sanskrit: yaiḥ āhataḥ śocati rātri ahāni
units.english: smitten by them one grieveth day and night.

units.sanskrit: parasya nā a marmasu te patanti tān paṇḍitaḥ na avasṛjet pareṣu
units.english: A learned man should not discharge such arrows, for do they not touch the very vitals of others.

units.sanskrit: yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam buddhim tasya apakarṣanti saḥ apācīnāni paśyati
units.english: He, to whom the gods ordain defeat, hath his senses taken away, and it is for this that he stoopeth to ignoble deeds.

units.sanskrit: buddhau kaluṣa bhūtāyām vināśe pratyupasthite anayaḥ naya saṃkāśaḥ hṛdayāt na apasarpati
units.english: When the intellect becometh dim and destruction is nigh, wrong, looking like right., firmly sticketh to the heart.

units.sanskrit: sā iyam buddhiḥ parītā te putrāṇām tava bhārata pāṇḍavānām virodhena na ca enām avabudhyase
units.english: Thou dost not clearly see it, O bull of the Bharata race, that clouded intellect hath now possessed thy sons in consequence of their hostility to the Pandavas.

units.sanskrit: rājā lakṣaṇa saṃpannaḥ trailokyasya api yaḥ bhavet
units.english: Endued with every auspicious mark and deserving to rule the three worlds, Yudhishthira is obedient to thy commands.

units.sanskrit: śiṣyaḥ te śāsitā saḥ astu dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ atīva sarvān putrān te bhāgadheya puraskṛtaḥ
units.english: Let him, O Dhritarashtra, rule the earth, to the exclusion of all thy sons, Yudhishthira is the foremost of all thy heirs.

units.sanskrit: gauravāt tava rāja indra bahūn kleśān titikṣati dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca brūhi bhūyas mahābuddhe dharma artha sahitam vacaḥ
units.english: Endued with energy and wisdom, and acquainted with the truths of religion and profit, Yudhishthira, that foremost of righteous men, hath, O king of kings, suffered much misery out of kindness and sympathy, in order to preserve thy reputation." SECTION XXXV "Dhritarashtra said, 'O thou of great intelligence, tell me again words such as these, consistent with religion and profit.

units.sanskrit: śṛṇvataḥ na asti me tṛptiḥ vicitrāṇi iha bhāṣase
units.english: My thirst for hearing them is not quenched.

units.sanskrit: viduraḥ uvāca sarva tīrtheṣu vā snānam sarva bhūteṣu ca ārjavam
units.english: What thou sayst is charming!" "Vidura said, 'Ablution in all the holy places and kindness to all creatures,--these two are equal.

units.sanskrit: ubhe ete same syātām ārjavam vā viśiṣyate
units.english: Perhaps, kindness to all creatures surpasseth the former.

units.sanskrit: ārjavam pratipadyasva putreṣu satatam vibho iha kīrtim parām prāpya pretya svargam avāpsyasi
units.english: O master, show kindness unto all thy sons, for by that winning great fame in this world, thou wilt have heaven hereafter.

units.sanskrit: yāvat kīrtiḥ manuṣyasya puṇyā lokeṣu gīyate tāvat sa puruṣa vyāghra svarga loke mahīyate
units.english: As long as a man's good deeds are spoken of in this world, so long, O tiger among men, is he glorified in heaven.

units.sanskrit: atra api udāharanti imam itihāsam purātanam virocanasya saṃvādam keśinī arthe sudhanvanā
units.english: In this connection is cited an old story about the conversation between Virochana and Sudhanwan, both suitors for Kesini's hand.

units.sanskrit: svayaṃvare sthitā kanyā keśinī nāma nāmataḥ rūpeṇa apratimā rājan viśiṣṭa pati kāmyayā
units.english: Once on a time, O king, there was a maiden of the name of Kesini, unrivalled for beauty; moved by the desire of obtaining a good husband, she resolved to choose her lord in Swayamvara.

units.sanskrit: virocanaḥ atha daiteyaḥ tadā tatra ājagāma ha prāptum icchan tatas tatra daitya indram prāha keśinī
units.english: Then one of the sons of Diti, Virochana by name, went to that spot, desirous of obtaining the maiden.

units.sanskrit: atha kena sma paryaṅkam sudhanvā na adhirohati virocanaḥ uvāca prājāpatyāḥ hi vai śreṣṭhāḥ vayam keśini sattamāḥ
units.english: Beholding that chief of the Daityas, Kesini addressed him, saying, 'Are Brahmanas superior, O Virochana, or are the sons of Diti superior? And why also should not Sudhanwan sit on the sofa?' Virochana said, 'Sprung from Prajapati himself, we, O Kesini, are the best and at the top of all creatures, and this world is ours without doubt.

units.sanskrit: asmākam khalu ime lokāḥ ke devāḥ ke dvijātayaḥ keśinī uvāca iha eva āssva pratīkṣāva upasthāne virocana
units.english: Who are the gods, and who are the Brahmanas?' Kesini said, 'We will, O Virochana, stay here in this very pavilion.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvā prātar āgantā paśyeyam vām samāgatau virocanaḥ uvāca tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā tvam bhīru bhāṣase
units.english: Sudhanwan will come here on the morrow, and let me see both of you sitting together.' Virochana said, 'O amiable and timid girl, I will do what thou sayst.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvānam ca mām ca eva prātar draṣṭāsi saṃgatau atītāyām ca śarvaryām udite sūrya maṇḍale atha ājagāma tam deśam sudhanvā rāja sattama
units.english: Thou wilt behold Sudhanwan and myself met together in the morning.' "Vidura continued, 'When the night had passed away and the solar disc had risen, Sudhanwan, O best of kings, came to that place where, O master, Virochana was waiting with Kesini.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvā ca samāgacchat prāhlādim keśinīm tathā
units.english: And Sudhanwan saw there both Prahlada's son and Kesini.

units.sanskrit: samāgatam dvijam dṛṣṭvā keśinī bharata ṛṣabha pratyutthāya āsanam tasmai pādyam arghyam dadau punar etasmin antare tatra sudhanvā pratyadṛśyata
units.english: And beholding the Brahmana arrived, Kesini, O bull of the Bharata race, rising up from hers, offered him a seat, water to wash his feet, and Arghya.

units.sanskrit: iti ha uvāca vacanam virocanam anuttamam sudhanvā uvāca anvālabhe hiraṇmayam prāhrāde aham tava āsanam
units.english: And asked by Virochana (to share his seat) Sudhanwan said, 'O son of Prahlada, I touch thy excellent golden seat.

units.sanskrit: eka tvam upasaṃpannaḥ na tu āseyam tvayā saha
units.english: I cannot, however, suffer myself to be regarded as thy equal, and sit on it with thee.' Virochana said, 'A piece of wooden plank, an animal skin, or a mat of grass or straw,--these only, O Sudhanwan, are fit for thee.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvan na tvam arhaḥ asi mayā saha samāsanam sudhanvā uvāca
units.english: Thou deservest not, however, the same seat with me.' Sudhanwan said, 'Father and son.

units.sanskrit: pitāputrau saha āsītām dvau viprau dvau ca pārthivau dvau ca eva vaiśyau śūdrau ca na tu anyau itaretaram
units.english: Brahmanas of the same age and equal learning, two Kshatriyas, two Vaisyas and two Sudras, can sit together on the same seat, Except these, no other can sit together.

units.sanskrit: pitā api te samāsīnam upāsīta eva mām adhas
units.english: Your father used to pay his regards to me, taking a seat lower than that occupied by me.

units.sanskrit: bālaḥ sukha edhitaḥ gehe na tvam kim cana budhyase virocanaḥ uvāca hiraṇyam ca gavāśvam ca yat vittam asureṣu naḥ
units.english: Thou art a child, brought tip in every luxury at home and thou understandest nothing.' Virochana said, 'Staking all the gold, kine, horses, and every other kind of wealth that we have among the Asuras, let us, O Sudhanwan, ask them this question that are able to answer.' Sudhanwan said, 'Let alone your gold, kine, and heroes, O Virochana? Making our lives forfeited, we will ask them this question that are competent.' Virochana said, 'Wagering our lives where shall we go? I will not appear before any of the gods and never before any among men.' Sudhanwan said, 'Having wagered our lives, we will approach thy father, for he, Prahlada, will never say an untruth even for the sake of his son.' "Vidura continued, 'Having thus laid a wager, Virochana and Sudhanwan, both moved by rage, proceeded to that place where Prahlada was.

units.sanskrit: prahrādaḥ uvāca imau tau saṃpradṛśyete yābhyām na caritam saha āśīviṣau iva kruddhau eka mārgam iha āgatau
units.english: And beholding them together, Prahlada said, 'These two who had never before been companions, are now seen together coming hither by the same road, like two angry snakes.

units.sanskrit: kim vai saha eva carataḥ na purā carataḥ saha tat tvām sudhanvan pṛcchāmi mā pṛṣṭam anṛtam vadīḥ virocana etat pṛcchāmi kim te sakhyam sudhanvanā
units.english: Have ye now become companions,--ye who were never companions before? I ask thee, O Virochana, has there been friendship between thee and Sudhanwan?' Virochana said, 'There is no friendship between me and Sudhanwan.

units.sanskrit: na me sudhanvanā sakhyam prāṇayoḥ vipaṇāvahe
units.english: On the other hand, we have both wagered our lives.

units.sanskrit: prahlāda praśnam anagham mūrdhnā te viphaliṣyati prahrādaḥ uvāca udakam madhuparkam ca api ānayantu sudhanvane
units.english: O chief of the Asuras, I shall ask thee a question, do not answer it untruly!' Prahlada said, 'Let water, and honey and curds, be brought for Sudhanwan.

units.sanskrit: brahman abhyarcanīyaḥ asi śvetā gauḥ pīvarīkṛtā
units.english: Thou deservest our worship, O Brahmana.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvā uvāca udakam madhuparkam ca pathaḥ eva arpitam mama
units.english: A white and fat cow is ready for thee.' Sudhanwan said, 'Water and honey and curds, have been presented to me on my way hither.

units.sanskrit: prahrāda tvam tu nau praśnam tathyam prabrūhi pṛcchatoḥ kim brāhmaṇāḥ svid śreyāṃsaḥ uta aho svid virocanaḥ
units.english: Prahlada, answer it truly! are Brahmanas superior, or is Virochana superior?' Prahlada said, O Brahmana, this one is my only son.

units.sanskrit: putraḥ vā anyaḥ bhavān brahman sākṣye ca eva bhavet sthitaḥ
units.english: Thou also art present here in person.

units.sanskrit: etat sudhanvan pṛcchāmi durvivaktā sma kim vaset
units.english: How can one like us answer a question about which ye two have quarrelled? Sudhanwan said, 'Give unto thy son thy kine and other precious wealth that thou mayst have, but, O wise one, thou shouldst declare the truth when we two are disputing about it.' Prahlada said, 'How doth that misuser of his tongue suffer, O Sudhanwan, who answereth not truly but falsely, a question that is put to him? I ask thee this.' Sudhanwan said, 'The person that misuseth his tongue suffers like the deserted wife, who pineth, at night, beholding her husband sleeping in the arms of a co-wife;

units.sanskrit: yām ca bhāra abhitapta aṅgaḥ durvivaktā sma tām vaset
units.english: like a person who hath lost at dice, or who is weighed down with an unbearable load of anxieties.

units.sanskrit: nagare pratiruddhaḥ san bahis dvāre bubhukṣitaḥ
units.english: Such a man hath also to stay, starving outside the citygates, into which his admission is barred.

units.sanskrit: sarva svena ca yaḥ hīnaḥ durvivaktā tu tām vaset
units.english: Indeed, he that giveth false evidence is destined to always find his foes.

units.sanskrit: pañca paśu anṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte
units.english: He that speaketh a lie on account of an animal, casteth down from heaven five of his sires of the ascending order. He that speaketh a lie on account of a cow casteth down from heaven ten of his ancestors.

units.sanskrit: śatam aśva anṛte hanti sahasram puruṣa anṛte
units.english: A lie on account of a horse causeth the downfall of a hundred; and a lie on account of a human being, the downfall of a thousand of one's sires of the ascending order.

units.sanskrit: hanti jātān ajātān ca hiraṇya arthe anṛtam vadan sarvam bhūmi anṛte hanti mā sma bhūmi anṛtam vadīḥ
units.english: An untruth on account of gold ruineth the members of one's race both born and unborn, while an untruth for the sake of land ruineth everything.

units.sanskrit: mattaḥ śreyān aṅgirāḥ vai sudhanvā tvat virocana
units.english: Therefore, never speak an untruth for the sake of land.' Prahlada said, 'Angiras is superior to myself, and Sudhanwan is superior to thee, O Virochana.

units.sanskrit: mātā asya śreyasī mātuḥ tasmāt tvam tena vai jitaḥ
units.english: Mother also of Sudhanwan is superior to thy mother; therefore, thou, O Virochana, hath been defeated by Sudhanwan.

units.sanskrit: virocana sudhanvā ayam prāṇānām īśvaraḥ tava
units.english: This Sudhanwan is now the master of thy life.

units.sanskrit: sudhanvan punar icchāmi tvayā dattam virocanam sudhanvā uvāca yat dharmam avṛṇīthāḥ tvam na kāmāt anṛtam vadīḥ
units.english: But, O Sudhanwan, I wish that thou shouldst grant Virochana his life.' Sudhanwan said, 'Since, O Prahlada, thou hast preferred virtue and hast not, from temptation, said an untruth, I grant thy son his life that is dear to thee.

units.sanskrit: eṣa prahrāda putraḥ te mayā dattaḥ virocanaḥ
units.english: So here is thy son Virochana, O Prahlada, restored by me to thee.

units.sanskrit: pāda prakṣālanam kuryāt kumāryāḥ saṃnidhau mama viduraḥ uvāca tasmāt rāja indra bhūmi arthe na anṛtam vaktum arhasi
units.english: He shall, however, have to wash my feet in the presence of the maiden Kesini.' "Vidura continued, 'For these reasons, O king of kings, it behoveth thee not to say an untruth for the sake of land.

units.sanskrit: mā gamaḥ sa suta amātyaḥ atyayam putrān anubhraman
units.english: Saying an untruth from affection for thy son, O king, hasten not to destruction, with all thy children and counsellors.

units.sanskrit: na devāḥ yaṣṭim ādāya rakṣanti paśupāla vat
units.english: The gods do not protect men, taking up clubs in their hands after the manner of herdsmen;

units.sanskrit: yam tu rakṣitum icchanti buddhyā saṃvibhajanti tam
units.english: unto those, however, they wish to protect, they grant intelligence.

units.sanskrit: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇe kurute manaḥ tathā tathā asya sarva arthāḥ sidhyante na atra saṃśayaḥ
units.english: There is no doubt that one's objects meet with success in proportion to the attention he directs to righteousness and morality.

units.sanskrit: māyāvinam māyayā vartamānam
units.english: The Vedas never rescue from sin a deceitful person living by falsehood.

units.sanskrit: nīḍam śakuntāḥ iva jāta pakṣāḥ chandāṃsi enam prajahati antakāle
units.english: On the other hand, they forsake him while he is on his death-bed, like newly fledged birds forsaking their nests.

units.sanskrit: matta apānam kalaham pūga vairam bhāryā patyoḥ antaram jñāti bhedam rāja dviṣṭam strī pumāṃsoḥ vivādam
units.english: Drinking, quarrels, enmity with large numbers of men, all connections with connubial disputes, and severance of relationship between husband and wife, internal dissensions, disloyalty to the king,--these and all paths that are sinful, should, it is said, be avoided.

units.sanskrit: sāmudrikam vaṇijam cora pūrvam śalākadhūrtam ca cikitsakam ca arim ca mitram ca kuśīlavam ca
units.english: A palmist, a thief turned into a merchant, a fowler, a physician, an enemy, a friend, and a minstrel, these seven are incompetent as witness.

units.sanskrit: māna agnihotram uta māna maunam mānena adhītam uta māna yajñaḥ etāni catvāri abhayaṃkarāṇi
units.english: An Agnihotra performed from motives of pride, abstention from speech, practised from similar motives, study and sacrifice from the same motives,--these four, of themselves innocent, become harmful when practised unduly.

units.sanskrit: agāra dāhī gara daḥ kuṇḍa āśī soma vikrayī parvakāraḥ ca sūcī ca mitradhruk pāradārikaḥ bhrūṇa hā guru talpī ca yaḥ ca syāt pānapaḥ dvijaḥ
units.english: One that setteth fire to a dwelling house, an administerer of poison, a pander, a vendor of the Soma-juice, a maker of arrows, an astrologer, one that injureth friends, an adulterer, one that causeth abortion, a violater of his preceptor's bed, a Brahmana addicted to drink, one that is sharp-speeched, a raker of old sores, an atheist, a reviler of the Vedas, and taker of bribes, one whose investiture with the sacred thread has been delayed beyond the prescribed age, one that secretly slayeth cattle, and one that slayeth him who prayeth for protection,--these all are reckoned as equal in moral turpitude as the slayers of Brahmanas.

units.sanskrit: tṛṇa ulkayā jñāyate jātarūpam
units.english: Gold is tested by fire;

units.sanskrit: yuge bhadraḥ vyavahāreṇa sādhuḥ
units.english: an honest man, by his conduct.

units.sanskrit: śūraḥ bhayeṣu artha kṛcchreṣu dhīraḥ
units.english: A brave man is tested during a season of panic; he that is self-controlled, in times of poverty;

units.sanskrit: kṛcchrāsu āpatsu suhṛdaḥ ca arayaḥ ca
units.english: and friends and foes, in times of calamity and danger.

units.sanskrit: jarā rūpam harati hi dhairyam āśā
units.english: Decrepitude destroyeth beauty;

units.sanskrit: mṛtyuḥ prāṇān dharma caryām asūyā krodhaḥ śriyam śīlam anārya sevā
units.english: ambitious hopes, patience; death, life, envy, righteousness, anger, prosperity, companionship with the low, good behaviour;

units.sanskrit: hriyam kāmaḥ sarvam eva abhimānaḥ
units.english: lust, modesty, and pride, everything.

units.sanskrit: śrīḥ maṅgalāt prabhavati prāgalbhyāt saṃpravardhate dākṣyāt tu kurute mūlam saṃyamāt pratitiṣṭhati
units.english: Prosperity taketh its birth in good deeds, groweth in consequence of activity, driveth its roots deep in consequence of skill, and acquireth stability owing to self-control.

units.sanskrit: aṣṭau guṇāḥ puruṣam dīpayanti prajñā ca kaulyam ca damaḥ śrutam ca parākramaḥ ca a bahu bhāṣitā ca
units.english: Wisdom, good lineage, self-control, acquaintance with the scriptures, prowess, absence of garrulity, gift to the extent of one's power, and grateful ness,--these eight qualities shed a lustre upon their possessor.

units.sanskrit: etān guṇān tāta mahā anubhāvān ekaḥ guṇaḥ saṃśrayate prasahya
units.english: But, O sire, there is one endowment which alone can cause all these attributes to come together;

units.sanskrit: rājā yadā satkurute manuṣyam sarvān guṇān eṣa guṇaḥ atibhāti
units.english: the fact is, when the king honoureth a particular person, the royal favour can cause all these attributes to shed their lustre (on the favourite).

units.sanskrit: aṣṭau nṛpa imāni manuṣya loke svargasya lokasya nidarśanāni catvāri eṣām anvavetāni sadbhiḥ
units.english: Those eight, O king, in the world of men, are indications of heaven.

units.sanskrit: catvāri eṣām anvavayanti santaḥ
units.english: Of the eight (mentioned below) four are inseparably connected, with the good, and four others are always followed by the good.

units.sanskrit: yajñaḥ dānam adhyayanam tapaḥ ca catvāri etāni anvavetāni sadbhiḥ damaḥ satyam ārjavam ānṛśaṃsyam
units.english: The first four which are inseparably connected with the good, are sacrifice, gift, study and asceticism, while the other four that are always followed by the good, are self-restraint, truth, simplicity, and abstention from injury to all.

units.sanskrit: catvāri etāni anvavayanti santaḥ ijyā adhyayana dānāni tapaḥ satyam kṣamā ghṛṇā alobhaḥ iti mārgaḥ ayam dharmasya aṣṭavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
units.english: 'Sacrifice, study, charity, asceticism, truth, forgiveness, mercy, and contentment constitute the eight different paths of righteousness.

units.sanskrit: tatra pūrva catur vargaḥ dambha artham api sevyate uttaraḥ tu catur vargaḥ na a mahātmasu tiṣṭhati
units.english: The first four of these may be practised from motives of pride, but the last four can exist only in those that are truly noble.

units.sanskrit: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā na te vṛddhāḥ ye na vadanti dharmam
units.english: That is no assembly where there are no old men, and they are not old who do not declare what morality is.

units.sanskrit: na asau dharmaḥ yatra na satyam asti na tat satyam yat chalena anuviddham
units.english: That is not morality which is separated from truth, and that is not truth which is fraught with deceit.

units.sanskrit: satyam rūpam śrutam vidyā kaulyam śīlam balam dhanam śauryam ca citra bhāṣyam ca daśa saṃsarga yonayaḥ
units.english: Truth, beauty, acquaintance with the scriptures, knowledge, high birth, good behaviour, strength, wealth, bravery, and capacity for varied talk,--these ten are of heavenly origin.

units.sanskrit: enaḥ gacchati kartāram nindā arhaḥ yatra nindyate pāpam kurvan pāpa kīrtiḥ pāpam eva aśnute phalam
units.english: A sinful person, by committing sin, is overtaken by evil consequences.

units.sanskrit: puṇyam kurvan puṇya kīrtiḥ puṇyam eva aśnute phalam
units.english: A virtuous man, by practising virtue, reapeth great happiness.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt pāpam na kurvīta puruṣaḥ śaṃsita vrataḥ
units.english: Therefore, a man, rigidly resolved, should abstain from sin.

units.sanskrit: pāpam prajñām nāśayati kriyamāṇam punar punar
units.english: Sin, repeatedly perpetrated, destroyeth intelligence;

units.sanskrit: naṣṭa prajñaḥ pāpam eva nityam ārabhate naraḥ
units.english: and the man who hath lost intelligence, repeatedly committeth sin.

units.sanskrit: puṇyam prajñām vardhayati kriyamāṇam punar punar
units.english: Virtue, repeatedly practised, enhanceth intelligence;

units.sanskrit: vṛddha prajñaḥ puṇyam eva nityam ārabhate naraḥ
units.english: and the man whose intelligence hath increased, repeatedly practiseth virtue.

units.sanskrit: puṇyam kurvan puṇya kīrtiḥ puṇyam sthānam sma gacchati
units.english: The virtuous man, by practising virtue, goeth to regions of blessedness.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt puṇyam niṣeveta puruṣaḥ su samāhitaḥ
units.english: Therefore, a man should, firmly resolved, practise virtue.

units.sanskrit: asūyakaḥ dandaśūkaḥ niṣṭhuraḥ vaira kṛt naraḥ sa kṛcchram mahat āpnoti nacirāt pāpam ācaran
units.english: He that is envious, he that injureth others deeply, he that is cruel, he that constantly quarreleth, he that is deceitful, soon meeteth with great misery for practising these sins.

units.sanskrit: anasūyaḥ kṛtaprajñaḥ śobhanāni ācaran sadā
units.english: He that is not envious and is possessed of wisdom, by always doing what is good, never meeteth with great misery;

units.sanskrit: pūjām ca mahatīm prāpya sa sarvatra virocate
units.english: on the other hand, he shineth everywhere.

units.sanskrit: prajñām eva āgamayati yaḥ prājñebhyaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ
units.english: He that draweth wisdom from them that are wise is really learned and wise.

units.sanskrit: prājñaḥ hi avāpya dharma arthau śaknoti sukham edhitum
units.english: And he that is wise, by attending to both virtue and profit, succeedeth in attaining to happiness.

units.sanskrit: divasena eva tat kuryāt yena rātrau sukham vaset
units.english: Do that during the day which may enable thee to pass the night in happiness;

units.sanskrit: aṣṭa māsena tat kuryāt yena varṣāḥ sukham vaset
units.english: and do that during eight months of the year which may enable thee to pass the season of rains happily.

units.sanskrit: pūrve vayasi tat kuryāt yena vṛddhaḥ sukham vaset
units.english: Do that during youth which may ensure a happy old age;

units.sanskrit: yāvat jīvena tat kuryāt yena pretya sukham vaset
units.english: and do that during thy whole life here which may enable thee to live happily hereafter.

units.sanskrit: jīrṇam annam praśaṃsanti bhāryām ca gata yauvanām śūram vigata saṃgrāmam gata pāram tapasvinam
units.english: The wise prize that food which is easily digested, that wife whose youth hath passed away, that hero who is victorious and that ascetic whose efforts have been crowned with success.

units.sanskrit: dhanena adharma labdhena yat chidram apidhīyate asaṃvṛtam tat bhavati tatas anyat avadīryate
units.english: The gap that is sought to be filled by wealth acquired wrongfully, remaineth uncovered, while new ones appear in other places.

units.sanskrit: guruḥ ātmavatām śāstā śāstā rājā durātmanām
units.english: The preceptor controlleth them whose souls are under their own control; the king controlleth persons that are wicked;

units.sanskrit: atha pracchanna pāpānām śāstā vaivasvataḥ yamaḥ
units.english: while they that sin secretly have their controller in Yama, the son of Vivaswat.

units.sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām ca nadīnām ca kulānām ca mahātmanām prabhavaḥ na adhigantavyaḥ strīṇām duścaritasya ca
units.english: The greatness of Rishis, of rivers, of river-banks, of high-souled men, and the cause of woman's wickedness, cannot be ascertained.

units.sanskrit: dvijāti pūjā abhirataḥ dātā jñātiṣu ca ārjavī kṣatriyaḥ svarga bhāj rājan ciram pālayate mahīm
units.english: O king, he that is devoted to the worship of the Brahmanas, he that giveth away, he that behaveth righteously towards his relatives, and the Kshatriya that behaveth nobly, rule the earth for ever.

units.sanskrit: suvarṇa puṣpām pṛthivīm cinvanti puruṣāḥ trayaḥ śūraḥ ca kṛta vidyaḥ ca yaḥ ca jānāti sevitum
units.english: He that is possessed of bravery, he that is possessed of learning, and he that knows how to protect others,--these three are always able to gather flowers of gold from the earth.

units.sanskrit: buddhi śreṣṭhāni karmāṇi bāhu madhyāni bhārata
units.english: Of acts, those accomplished by intelligence are first; those accomplished by the arms, second;

units.sanskrit: tāni jaṅghā jaghanyāni bhāra pratyavarāṇi ca
units.english: those by the thighs, and those by bearing weights upon the head, are the very worst.

units.sanskrit: duryodhane ca śakunau mūḍhe duḥśāsane tathā karṇe ca aiśvaryam ādhāya katham tvam bhūtim icchasi sarvaiḥ guṇaiḥ upetāḥ ca pāṇḍavāḥ bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: Reposing the care of thy kingdom on Duryodhana, on Sakuni, on foolish Dussasana, and on Karna, how canst thou hope for prosperity? Possessed of every virtue, the Pandavas, O bull of the Bharata race, depend on thee as their father.

units.sanskrit: pitṛ vat tvayi vartante teṣu vartasva putra vat viduraḥ uvāca atra eva udāharanti imam itihāsam purātanam
units.english: O, repose thou on them as on thy sons!" SECTION XXXVI "Vidura said, 'In this connection is cited the old story of the discourse between the son of Atri and the deities called Sadhyas is as heard by us.

units.sanskrit: carantam haṃsa rūpeṇa mahā ṛṣim saṃśita vratam sādhyāḥ devāḥ mahā prājñam paryapṛcchanta vai purā
units.english: In days of old, the deities known by the name of Sadhyas questioned the highly wise and great Rishi of rigid vows (the son of Atri), while the latter was wandering in the guise of one depending on eleemosynary charity for livelihood.

units.sanskrit: sādhyāḥ devāḥ vayam asmaḥ mahā ṛṣe
units.english: The Sadhyas said, 'We are, O great Rishi, deities known as Sadhyas.

units.sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhavantam na śaknumaḥ anumātum
units.english: Beholding thee, we are unable to guess who thou art.

units.sanskrit: śrutena dhīraḥ buddhimān tvam mataḥ naḥ
units.english: It seemeth to us, however, that thou art possessed of intelligence and self-control in consequence of acquaintance with the scriptures.

units.sanskrit: etat kāryam amarāḥ saṃśrutam me dhṛtiḥ śamaḥ satya dharma anuvṛttiḥ granthim vinīya hṛdayasya sarvam
units.english: It, therefore, behoveth thee to discourse to us in magnanimous words fraught with learning.' The mendicant Rishi answered, 'Ye immortals, it hath been heard by me that by untying all the knots in the heart by the aid of tranquillity, and by mastery over all the passions, and observance of true religion, one should regard both the agreeable and the disagreeable like his own self.

units.sanskrit: ākruśyamānaḥ na ākrośet manyuḥ eva titikṣitaḥ
units.english: One should not return the slanders or reproaches of others for the pain that is felt by him who beareth silently, consumeth the slanderer;

units.sanskrit: ākroṣṭāram nirdahati sukṛtam ca asya vindati
units.english: and he that beareth, succeedeth also in appropriating the virtues of the slanderer.

units.sanskrit: na ākrośī syāt na avamānī parasya
units.english: Indulge not in slanders and reproaches. Do not humiliate and insult others.

units.sanskrit: mitra drohī na uta nīca upasevī
units.english: Quarrel not with friends.

units.sanskrit: na ca atimānī na ca hīna vṛttaḥ
units.english: Be not arrogant and ignoble in conduct.

units.sanskrit: rūkṣām vācam ruśatīm varjayīta
units.english: Avoid words that are harsh and fraught with anger.

units.sanskrit: marmāṇi asthīni hṛdayam tathā asūn ghorāḥ vācaḥ nirdahanti iha puṃsām
units.english: Harsh words burn and scorch the very vitals, bones, heart, and the very sources of the life of men.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt vācam ruśatīm rūkṣa rūpām dharma ārāmaḥ nityaśas varjayīta aruṃtudam paruṣam rūkṣa vācam
units.english: Therefore, he, that is virtuous, should always abstain from harsh and angry words.

units.sanskrit: vāc kaṇṭakaiḥ vitudantam manuṣyān
units.english: That worst of men is of harsh and wrathful speech, who pierceth the vitals of others with wordy thorns, beareth hell in his tongue, and should ever be regarded as a dispenser of misery to men.

units.sanskrit: bhṛśam su tīkṣṇaiḥ anala arka dīptaiḥ viricyamānaḥ api atiricyamānaḥ vidyāt kaviḥ su kṛtam me dadhāti
units.english: The man that is wise, pierced by another's wordy arrows, sharp-pointed and smarting like fire or the sun, should, even if deeply wounded and burning with pain, bear them patiently remembering that the slanderer's merits become his.

units.sanskrit: vāsaḥ yathā raṅga vaśam prayāti
units.english: He that waiteth upon one that is good or upon one that is wicked, upon one that is possessed of ascetic merit or upon one that is a thief, soon taketh the colour from that companion of his, like a cloth from the dye in which it is soaked.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ na ahataḥ pratihanyāt na ghātayet yaḥ hantu kāmasya na pāpam icchet tasmai devāḥ spṛhayanti āgatāya
units.english: The very gods desire his company, who, stung with reproach, returneth if not himself nor causeth others to return it, or who being struck doth not himself return the blow nor causeth other to do it, and who wisheth not the slightest injury to him that injureth him.

units.sanskrit: a vyāhṛtam vyāhṛtāt śreyaḥ āhuḥ
units.english: Silence, it is said, is better than speech, if speak you must, then it is better to say the truth;

units.sanskrit: satyam vadet vyāhṛtam tat dvitīyam priyam vadet vyāhṛtam tat tṛtīyam
units.english: if truth is to be said, it is better to say what is agreeable;

units.sanskrit: dharmyam vadet vyāhṛtam tat caturtham
units.english: and if what is agreeable is to be said, then it is better to say what is consistent with morality.

units.sanskrit: yādṛśaiḥ saṃvivadate yādṛśān ca upasevate yādṛś icchet ca bhavitum tādṛś bhavati pūruṣaḥ
units.english: A man becometh exactly like him with whom he liveth, or like him whom he regardeth, or like that which he wisheth to be.

units.sanskrit: yatas yatas nivartate tatas tatas vimucyate nivartanāt hi sarvatas na vetti duḥkham aṇu api
units.english: One is freed from those things from which one abstaineth, and if one abstaineth from everything he hath not to suffer even the least misery.

units.sanskrit: na jīyate na uta jigīṣate anyān
units.english: Such a man neither vanquisheth others, nor is vanquished by others.

units.sanskrit: na vaira kṛt ca apratighātakaḥ ca
units.english: He never injureth nor opposeth others.

units.sanskrit: nindā praśaṃsāsu sama svabhāvaḥ
units.english: He is unmoved by praise or blame.

units.sanskrit: na śocate hṛṣyati na eva ca ayam
units.english: He neither grieveth nor exalteth in joy.

units.sanskrit: bhāvam icchati sarvasya na abhāve kurute matim satya vādī mṛduḥ dāntaḥ yaḥ saḥ uttama pūruṣaḥ
units.english: That man is regarded as a mediocre in goodness who never consoleth others by saying what is not true;

units.sanskrit: na anarthakam sāntvayati pratijñāya dadāti ca
units.english: who giveth having promise;

units.sanskrit: rāddha aparāddhe jānāti yaḥ sa madhyama pūruṣaḥ
units.english: and who keepeth an eye over the weakness of others.

units.sanskrit: duḥśāsanaḥ tu upahantā na śāstā
