units.english: These, however, are the indications of a bad man, viz., incapacity to be controlled;

units.sanskrit: na āvartate manyu vaśāt kṛtaghnaḥ
units.english: proneness to give way to wrath, ungratefulness;

units.sanskrit: na kasya cit mitram atho durātmā
units.english: inability to become another's friend, and wickedness of heart.

units.sanskrit: na śraddadhāti kalyāṇam parebhyaḥ api ātma śaṅkitaḥ nirākaroti mitrāṇi yaḥ vai saḥ adhama pūruṣaḥ
units.english: He too is the worst of men, who is dissatisfied with any good that may come to him from others who is suspicious of his own self, and who driveth away from himself all his true friends.

units.sanskrit: uttamān eva seveta prāpte kāle tu madhyamān adhamān tu na seveta yaḥ icchet śreyaḥ ātmanaḥ
units.english: He that desireth prosperity to himself, should wait upon them that are good, and at times upon them that are indifferent, but never upon them that are bad.

units.sanskrit: na tu eva samyak labhate praśaṃsām na vṛttam āpnoti mahā kulānām dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca
units.english: He that is wicked, earneth wealth, it is true, by putting forth his strength, by constant effort, by intelligence, and by prowess, but he can never win honest fame, nor can he acquire the virtues and manners of high families (in any of which he may be born).' "Dhritarashtra said, 'The gods, they that regard both virtue and profit without swerving from either, and they that are possessed of great learning, express a liking for high families.

units.sanskrit: bhavanti vai kāni mahā kulāni viduraḥ uvāca tapaḥ damaḥ brahma vid tvam vitānāḥ
units.english: I ask thee, O Vidura, this question,--what are those families that are called high?' "Vidura said, 'Asceticism, self-restraint, knowledge of the Vedas, sacrifices, pure marriages, and gifts of food,--those families in which these seven exist or are practised duly, are regarded as high.

units.sanskrit: yeṣām na vṛttam vyathate na yoniḥ vṛtta prasādena caranti dharmam ye kīrtim icchanti kule viśiṣṭām
units.english: There are high families who deviate not from the right course whose deceased ancestors are never pained (by witnessing the wrong-doings of their descendants), who cheerfully practise all the virtues, who desire to enhance the pure fame of the line in which they are born, and who avoid every kind of falsehood.

units.sanskrit: anijyayā avivāhaiḥ ca vedasya utsādanena ca kulāni akula tām yānti dharmasya atikrameṇa ca deva dravya vināśena brahma sva haraṇena ca
units.english: Families that are high, fall down and become low owing to the absence of sacrifices, impure marriages, abandonment of the Vedas, and insults offered to Brahmanas.

units.sanskrit: kulāni akula tām yānti brāhmaṇa atikrameṇa ca brāhmaṇānām paribhavāt parivādāt ca bhārata kulāni akula tām yānti nyāsa apaharaṇena ca
units.english: High families fall off and become low owing to their members disregarding or speaking ill of Brahmanas, or to the misappropriation, O Bharata, of what had been deposited with them by others.

units.sanskrit: kulāni samupetāni gobhiḥ puruṣataḥ aśvataḥ kula saṃkhyām na gacchanti yāni hīnāni vṛttataḥ vṛttataḥ tu avihīnāni kulāni alpa dhanāni api
units.english: Those families that are possessed of members, wealth and kine, are not regarded as families if they be wanting in good manners and conduct, while families wanting in wealth but distinguished by manners and good conduct are regarded as such and win great reputation.

units.sanskrit: vṛttam yatnena saṃrakṣet vittam eti ca yāti ca
units.english: Therefore, should good manners and good conduct be maintained with care, for, as regards wealth, it cometh or goeth.

units.sanskrit: akṣīṇaḥ vittataḥ kṣīṇaḥ vṛttataḥ tu hataḥ hataḥ
units.english: He that is wanting in wealth is not really wanting, but he that is wanting in manners and conduct is really in want.

units.sanskrit: gobhiḥ paśubhiḥ aśvaiḥ ca kṛṣyā ca su samṛddhayā kulāni na prarohanti yāni hīnāni vṛttataḥ
units.english: Those families that abound in kine and other cattle and in the produce of the field are not really worthy of regard and fame if they be wanting in manners and conduct.

units.sanskrit: mā naḥ kule vaira kṛt kaḥ cit astu rāja amātyaḥ mā parasva apahārī mitra drohī naikṛtikaḥ anṛtī vā
units.english: Let none in our race be a fomenter of quarrels, none serve a king as minister, none steal the wealth of others, none provoke intestine dissensions, none be deceitful or false in behaviour, and none eat before serving the Rishis, the gods, and guests.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca naḥ brāhmaṇam hanyāt yaḥ ca naḥ brāhmaṇān dviṣet na naḥ sa samitim gacchet yaḥ ca naḥ nirvapet kṛṣim
units.english: He, in our race, who slayeth Brahmanas, or entertaineth feelings of aversion towards them, or impedeth or otherwise injureth agriculture, doth not deserve to mix with us.

units.sanskrit: tṛṇāni bhūmiḥ udakam vāc caturthī ca sūnṛtā satām etāni geheṣu na ucchidyante kadā cana
units.english: Straw (for a seat), ground (for sitting upon), water (to wash the feet and face), and, fourthly sweet words,--these are never wanting in the houses of the good.

units.sanskrit: pravṛttāni mahā prājña dharmiṇām puṇya karmaṇām
units.english: Virtuous men devoted to the practice of righteous acts, when desirous of entertaining (guests), have these things ready for being offered with reverence.

units.sanskrit: sūkṣmaḥ api bhāram nṛpate syandanaḥ vai
units.english: As the Sandal tree, O king, though thin, is competent to bear weights which timbers of other trees (much thicker) cannot;

units.sanskrit: evam yuktāḥ bhāra sahāḥ bhavanti
units.english: so they that belong to high families are always able to bear the weight of great cares which ordinary men cannot.

units.sanskrit: na tat mitram yasya kopāt bibheti
units.english: He is no friend whose anger inspireth fear, or who is to be waited upon with fear.

units.sanskrit: yat vā mitram śaṅkitena upacaryam yasmin mitre pitari iva āśvasīta
units.english: He, however, on whom one can repose confidence as on a father, is a true friend.

units.sanskrit: tat vai mitram saṃgatāni itarāṇi
units.english: Other friendships are nominal connection.

units.sanskrit: saḥ eva bandhuḥ tat mitram sā gatiḥ tad parāyaṇam
units.english: He that beareth himself as a friend, even though unconnected by birth of blood, is a true friend, a real refuge, and a protector.

units.sanskrit: cala cittasya vai puṃsaḥ vṛddhān an upasevataḥ pāriplava mateḥ nityam adhruvaḥ mitra saṃgrahaḥ
units.english: He, whose heart is unsteady, or who doth not wait upon the aged, or who is of a restless disposition cannot make friends.

units.sanskrit: cala cittam anātmānam indriyāṇām vaśa anugam arthāḥ samativartante haṃsāḥ śuṣkam saraḥ yathā
units.english: Success (in the attainment of objects) forsaketh the person whose heart is unsteady, or who hath no control over his mind, or who is a slave of his senses, like swans forsaking a tank whose waters have dried up.

units.sanskrit: akasmāt eva kupyanti prasīdanti animittataḥ
units.english: They that are of weak minds suddenly give way to anger and are gratified without sufficient cause;

units.sanskrit: śīlam etat asādhūnām abhram pāriplavam yathā
units.english: they are like clouds that are so inconstant.

units.sanskrit: satkṛtāḥ ca kṛtārthāḥ ca mitrāṇām na bhavanti ye tān mṛtān api kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnān na upabhuñjate
units.english: The very birds of prey abstain from touching the dead bodies of those who having been served and benefited by friends, show ingratitude to the latter.

units.sanskrit: arthayet eva mitrāṇi sati vā asati vā dhane
units.english: Beest thou poor or beest thou rich, thou shouldst honour thy friends.

units.sanskrit: na anarthayan vijānāti mitrāṇām sāra phalgu tām
units.english: Until some service is asked, the sincerity or otherwise of friends cannot be known.

units.sanskrit: saṃtāpāt bhraśyate rūpam saṃtāpāt bhraśyate balam
units.english: sorrow killeth strength;

units.sanskrit: saṃtāpāt bhraśyate jñānam saṃtāpāt vyādhim ṛcchati
units.english: sorrow killeth the understanding; and sorrow bringeth on disease.

units.sanskrit: an avāpyam ca śokena śarīram ca upatapyate
units.english: Grief, instead of helping the acquisition of his object, drieth up the body, and maketh one's foes glad.

units.sanskrit: punar naraḥ mriyate jāyate ca
units.english: Therefore, do not yield to grief, Men repeatedly die and are reborn;

units.sanskrit: punar naraḥ hīyate vardhate punar
units.english: repeatedly they wither away and grow;

units.sanskrit: punar naraḥ yācati yācyate ca
units.english: repeatedly they ask others for help, and they themselves are asked for help;

units.sanskrit: punar naraḥ śocati śocyate punar
units.english: repeatedly they lament and are lamented.

units.sanskrit: sukham ca duḥkham ca bhava abhavau ca lābha alābhau maraṇam jīvitam ca paryāyaśaḥ sarvam iha spṛśanti
units.english: Happiness and misery, plenty and want, gain and loss, life and death, are shared by all in due order.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt dhīraḥ na eva hṛṣyet na śocet
units.english: Therefore, he that is self-controlled should neither exult in joy nor repine in sorrow.

units.sanskrit: calāni hi imāni ṣaḍ indriyāṇi
units.english: The six senses are always restless.

units.sanskrit: tatas tatas sravate buddhiḥ asya chidra uda kumbhāt iva nityam ambhaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca
units.english: Through the most predominant one amongst them one's understanding escapeth in proportion to the strength it assumes, like water from a pot through its holes.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'King Yudhishthira who is like a flame of fire, has been deceived by me.

units.sanskrit: mandānām mama putrāṇām yuddhena antam kariṣyati
units.english: He will surely exterminate in battle all my wicked sons.

units.sanskrit: nitya udvignam idam sarvam nitya udvignam idam manaḥ yat tat padam anudvignam tat me vada mahāmate viduraḥ uvāca
units.english: Everything, therefore, seems to me to be fraught with danger, and my mind is full of anxiety, O thou of great intelligence, tell me such words as may dispel my anxiety.' "Vidura said, 'O sinless one, in nothing else than knowledge and asceticism, in nothing else than restraining the senses, in nothing else than complete abandonment of avarice, do I see thy good.

units.sanskrit: buddhyā bhayam praṇudati tapasā vindate mahat
units.english: Fear is dispelled by self-knowledge; by asceticism one winneth what is great and valuable;

units.sanskrit: guru śuśrūṣayā jñānam śāntim tyāgena vindati
units.english: by waiting upon superiors learning is acquired; and peace is gained by self-restraint.

units.sanskrit: anāśritāḥ dāna puṇyam veda puṇyam anāśritāḥ rāga dveṣa vinirmuktāḥ vicaranti iha mokṣiṇaḥ
units.english: They that desire salvation without having acquired the merit attainable by gifts, or that which is attainable by practising the ritual of the Vedas, do not sojourn through life, freed from anger and aversion.

units.sanskrit: su adhītasya su yuddhasya su kṛtasya ca karmaṇaḥ tapasaḥ ca su taptasya tasya ante sukham edhate
units.english: The happiness that may be derived from a judicious course of study, from a battle fought virtuously, from ascetic austerities performed rigidly, always increaseth at the end.

units.sanskrit: su āstīrṇāni śayanāni prapannā na vai bhinnāḥ jātu nidrām labhante
units.english: They that are no longer in peace with their relatives, obtain no steep even if they have recourse to well-made beds;

units.sanskrit: na strīṣu rājan ratim āpnuvanti na māgadhaiḥ stūyamānāḥ na sūtaiḥ
units.english: nor do they, O king, derive any plea. sure from women, or the laudatory hymns of bards and eulogists.

units.sanskrit: na vai bhinnāḥ jātu caranti dharmam
units.english: Such persons can never practise virtue.

units.sanskrit: na vai sukham prāpnuvanti iha bhinnāḥ
units.english: Happiness can never be theirs, in this world.

units.sanskrit: na vai bhinnāḥ praśamam rocayanti
units.english: Honours can never be theirs, and peace hath no charm for them.

units.sanskrit: yogakṣemam kalpate na uta teṣām
units.english: Counsels that are for their benefit please them not.

units.sanskrit: na vidyate kim cit anyat vināśāt
units.english: They never acquire what they have not, nor succeed in retaining what they have, O king, there is no other end for such men save destruction.

units.sanskrit: saṃbhāvyam goṣu saṃpannam saṃbhāvyam brāhmaṇe tapaḥ saṃbhāvyam strīṣu cāpalyam saṃbhāvyam jñātitaḥ bhayam
units.english: As milk is possible in kine, asceticism in Brahmanas, and inconstancy in women, so fear is possible from relatives.

units.sanskrit: tantavaḥ api āyatāḥ nityam tantavaḥ bahulāḥ samāḥ bahūn bahu tvāt āyāsān sahanti iti upamā satām
units.english: Numerous thin threads of equal length, collected together, are competent to bear, from the strength of numbers, the constant rolling of the shuttle-cock over them.

units.sanskrit: dhūmāyante vyapetāni jvalanti sahitāni ca
units.english: but brought together they blaze forth into a powerful flame.

units.sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra ulmukāni iva jñātayaḥ bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: The case is even so, O Dhritarashtra, with relatives.

units.sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca ye śūrāḥ strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca vṛntāt iva phalam pakvam dhṛtarāṣṭra patanti te
units.english: They, O Dhritarashtra, who tyrannise over Brahmanas, women, relatives, and kine, soon fall off their stalks, like fruits that are ripe.

units.sanskrit: mahān api ekajaḥ vṛkṣaḥ balavān su pratiṣṭhitaḥ prasahya eva vātena śākhā skandham vimarditum
units.english: And the tree that stands singly, though gigantic and strong and deep-rooted, hath its trunk soon smashed and twisted by a mighty wind.

units.sanskrit: atha ye sahitāḥ vṛkṣāḥ saṃghaśas su pratiṣṭhitāḥ te hi śīghratamān vātān sahante anyonya saṃśrayāt
units.english: Those trees, however, that grow in close compact are competent owing to mutual dependence to resist winds more violent still.

units.sanskrit: evam manuṣyam api ekam guṇaiḥ api samanvitam śakyam dviṣantaḥ manyante vāyuḥ drumam iva ekajam
units.english: Thus he that is single, however, endowed with all the virtues, is regarded by foes as capable of being vanquished like an isolated tree by the wind.

units.sanskrit: anyonya samupaṣṭambhāt anyonya apāśrayeṇa ca jñātayaḥ saṃpravardhante sarasi iva utpalāni uta
units.english: Relatives, again, in consequence of mutual dependence and mutual aid, grow together, like lotus-stalks in a lake.

units.sanskrit: avadhyāḥ brāhmaṇāḥ gāvaḥ striyaḥ bālāḥ ca jñātayaḥ yeṣām ca annāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇa āgatāḥ
units.english: These must never be slain, viz., Brahmanas, kine, relatives, children, women, those whose food is eaten, and those also that yield by asking for protection.

units.sanskrit: na manuṣye guṇaḥ kaś cid anyaḥ dhanavatām api
units.english: O king, without wealth no good quality can show itself in a person.

units.sanskrit: an ātura tvāt bhadram te mṛta kalpāḥ hi rogiṇaḥ
units.english: If, however, thou art in health, thou canst achieve thy good, for he is dead who is unhealthy and ill.

units.sanskrit: avyādhi jam kaṭukam śīrṣa rogam pāpa anubandham paruṣam tīkṣṇam ugram satām peyam yat na pibanti asantaḥ
units.english: O king, anger is a kind of bitter, pungent, acrid, and hot drink, painful in its consequences: it is a kind of headache not born of any physical illness, and they that are unwise can never digest it.

units.sanskrit: manyum mahā rāja piba praśāmya
units.english: Do thou, O king, swallow it up and obtain peace.

units.sanskrit: roga arditāḥ na phalāni ādriyante
units.english: They that are tortured by disease have no liking for enjoyments, nor do they desire any happiness from wealth.

units.sanskrit: na vai labhante viṣayeṣu tattvam duḥkha upetāḥ rogiṇaḥ nityam eva na budhyante dhana bhogān na saukhyam
units.english: The sick, however, filled with sorrow, know not what happiness is or what the enjoyments of wealth are.

units.sanskrit: purā hi uktaḥ na akaroḥ tvam vacaḥ me dyūte jitām draupadīm prekṣya rājan
units.english: Beholding Draupadi won at dice, I told thee before, O king, these words,--They that are honest avoid deceit in play.

units.sanskrit: duryodhanam vāraya iti akṣavatyām
units.english: Therefore, stop Duryodhana! Thou didst not, however, act according to my words.

units.sanskrit: na tat balam yat mṛdunā virudhyate
units.english: That is not strength which is opposed to softness.

units.sanskrit: miśraḥ dharmaḥ tarasā sevitavyaḥ
units.english: On the other hand, strength mixed with softness constitutes true policy which should ever be pursued.

units.sanskrit: pradhvaṃsinī krūra samāhitā śrīḥ
units.english: That prosperity which is dependent on crookedness alone is destined to be destroyed.

units.sanskrit: mṛdu prauḍhā gacchati putra pautrān
units.english: That prosperity, however, which depends on both strength and softness, descends to sons and grandsons in tact.

units.sanskrit: pāṇḍoḥ sutāḥ tava putrān ca pāntu
units.english: Let, therefore, thy sons cherish the Pandavas, and the Pandavas also cherish thy sons.

units.sanskrit: eka ari mitrāḥ kuravaḥ hi eka mantrā jīvantu rājan sukhinaḥ samṛddhāḥ
units.english: O king, let the Kurus and the Pandavas, both having same friends and same foes, live together in happiness and prosperity.

units.sanskrit: meḍhī bhūtaḥ kauravāṇām tvam adya
units.english: Thou art, today, O king, the refuge of the sons of Kuru.

units.sanskrit: tvayi ādhīnam kuru kulam ājamīḍha
units.english: Indeed, the race of Kuru, O Ajamida, is dependent on thee.

units.sanskrit: pārthān bālān vana vāsa prataptān
units.english: O sire, preserving thy fame unsullied, cherish thou the children of Pandu, afflicted as they are with the sufferings of exile.

units.sanskrit: saṃdhatsva tvam kauravān pāṇḍu putraiḥ
units.english: O descendant of Kuru, make peace with the sons of Pandu.

units.sanskrit: mā te antaram ripavaḥ prārthayantu
units.english: Let not thy foes discover thy holes.

units.sanskrit: satye sthitāḥ te naradeva sarve
units.english: They all, O god among men, are devoted to truth.

units.sanskrit: saptadaśa imān rāja indra manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvaḥ abravīt vaicitravīrya puruṣān ākāśam muṣṭibhiḥ ghnataḥ tān eva indrasya hi dhanuḥ anāmyam namataḥ abravīt
units.english: O king of men, withdraw Duryodhana from his evil ways.'" SECTION XXXVII "Vidura said, 'O son of Vichitravirya, Manu, the son of the Self-created, hath, O king, spoken of the following seven and ten kinds of men, as those that strike empty space with their fists, or seek to bend the vapoury bow of Indra in the sky, or desire to catch the intangible rays of the sun.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca a śiṣyam śāsati yaḥ ca kupyate
units.english: he who is content with small gains;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca ativelam bhajate dviṣantam
units.english: he who humbly pays court to enemies;

units.sanskrit: striyaḥ ca yaḥ arakṣati bhadram astu te
units.english: he who seeks to restrain women's frailty;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca a yācyam yācati yaḥ ca katthate
units.english: he who asketh him for gifts who should never be asked; he who boasteth, having done anything;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca abhijātaḥ prakaroti akāryam
units.english: he who, born in a high family, perpetrateth an improper deed;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca abalaḥ balinā nitya vairī
units.english: he who being weak always wageth hostilities with one that is powerful;

units.sanskrit: aśraddadhānāya ca yaḥ bravīti
units.english: he who talketh to a person listening scoffingly;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca akāmyam kāmayate narendra
units.english: he who desireth to have that which is unattainable;

units.sanskrit: vadhvā hāsam śvaśuraḥ yaḥ ca manyate
units.english: he who being a father-in-law, jesteth with his daughter-in-law;

units.sanskrit: vadhvā vasan uta yaḥ māna kāmaḥ
units.english: he who boasteth at having his alarms dispelled by his daughter-in-law;

units.sanskrit: para kṣetre nirvapati yaḥ ca bījam
units.english: he who scattereth his own seeds in another's field;

units.sanskrit: striyam ca yaḥ parivadate ativelam
units.english: he who speaketh ill of his own wife;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ ca eva labdhvā na smarāmi iti uvāca dattvā ca yaḥ katthati yācyamānaḥ yaḥ ca asataḥ sāntvam upāsati iha
units.english: he who having received anything from another sayeth that he doth not remember it, he who, having given away anything in words in holy places, boasteth at home when asked to make good his words, and he who striveth to prove the truth of what is false.

units.sanskrit: ete anuyānti anilam pāśa hastāḥ
units.english: The envoys of Yama, with nooses in hand, drag those persons to hell.

units.sanskrit: yasmin yathā vartate yaḥ manuṣyaḥ
units.english: One should behave towards another just as that other behaveth towards him.

units.sanskrit: tasmin tathā vartitavyam sa dharmaḥ
units.english: Even this is consistent with social polity.

units.sanskrit: māyā ācāraḥ māyayā vartitavyaḥ
units.english: One may behave deceitfully towards him that behaveth deceitfully, but honestly towards him that is honest in his behaviour.

units.sanskrit: jarā rūpam harati hi dhairyam āśā
units.english: Old age killeth beauty; patience, hope;

units.sanskrit: mṛtyuḥ prāṇān dharma caryām asūyā
units.english: death, life; the practice of virtue, worldly enjoyments;

units.sanskrit: kāmaḥ hriyam vṛttam anārya sevā
units.english: lust, modesty;

units.sanskrit: krodhaḥ śriyam sarvam eva abhimānaḥ
units.english: anger, prosperity;

units.sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca śatāyuḥ uktaḥ puruṣaḥ sarva vedeṣu vai yadā
units.english: and pride, everything.' "Dhritarashtra said, 'Man hath been spoken of in all the Vedas as having hundred years for the period of his life.

units.sanskrit: na āpnoti atha ca tat sarvam āyuḥ kena iha hetunā viduraḥ uvāca ativādaḥ atimānaḥ ca tathā atyāgaḥ narādhipa
units.english: For what reason then, do not all men attain the allotted period?' "Vidura said, 'Excess of pride, excess in speech, excess in eating, anger, the desire of enjoyment, and intestine dissensions,--these, O king, are six sharp swords that cut off the period of life allotted to creatures.

units.sanskrit: ete eva asayaḥ tīkṣṇāḥ kṛntanti āyūṃṣi dehinām etāni mānavān ghnanti na mṛtyuḥ bhadram astu te
units.english: It is these which kill men, and not death.

units.sanskrit: viśvastasya eti yaḥ dārān yaḥ ca api guru talpa gaḥ
units.english: Knowing this, blessed be thou!' 'He who appropriates to himself the wife of one who hath confided in him; he who violates the bed of his preceptor;

units.sanskrit: vṛṣalī patiḥ dvijaḥ yaḥ ca pānapaḥ ca eva bhārata
units.english: that Brahmana, O Bharata, who becomes the husband of a Sudra woman, or drinks wines;

units.sanskrit: ādeśa kṛt vṛtti hantā dvijānām preṣakaḥ ca yaḥ
units.english: he who commendeth Brahmanas or becometh their master, or taketh away the lands that support them;

units.sanskrit: śaraṇa āgata hā ca eva sarve brahma haṇaiḥ samāḥ
units.english: and he who taketh the lives of those who yield asking for protection, are all guilty of the sin of slaying Brahmanas.

units.sanskrit: etaiḥ sametya kartavyam prāyaścittam iti śrutiḥ
units.english: The Vedas declare that contact with these requires expiation.

units.sanskrit: gṛhī vadānyaḥ anapaviddha vākyaḥ
units.english: He that accepts the teaching of the wise;

units.sanskrit: śeṣa anna bhoktā api avihiṃsakaḥ ca
units.english: he that envieth none;

units.sanskrit: na anartha kṛt tyakta kaliḥ kṛtajñaḥ
units.english: he that is incapable of doing anything that injureth others;

units.sanskrit: satyaḥ mṛduḥ svargam upaiti vidvān
units.english: he that is grateful, truthful, humble and learned, succeedeth in attaining to heaven.

units.sanskrit: sulabhāḥ puruṣāḥ rājan satatam priya vādinaḥ
units.english: 'They are abundant, O king, that can always speak agreeable words.

units.sanskrit: apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
units.english: The speaker, however, is rare, as also the hearer, of words that are disagreeable but medicinal.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ hi dharmam vyapāśritya hitvā bhartuḥ priya apriye
units.english: That man who, without regarding what is agreeable or disagreeable to his master but keeping virtue alone in view, sayeth what is unpalatable, but medicinal, truly addeth to the strength of the king.

units.sanskrit: tyajet kula arthe puruṣam grāmasya arthe kulam tyajet
units.english: For the sake of the family a member may be sacrificed; for the sake of the village, a family may be sacrificed;

units.sanskrit: grāmam janapadasya arthe ātma arthe pṛthivīm tyajet
units.english: for the sake of a kingdom a village may be sacrificed; and for the sake of one's soul, the whole earth may be sacrificed.

units.sanskrit: āpad artham dhanam rakṣet dārān rakṣet dhanaiḥ api
units.english: One should protect his wealth in view of the calamities that may overtake him;

units.sanskrit: ātmānam satatam rakṣet dāraiḥ api dhanaiḥ api
units.english: by his wealth one should protect his wives, and by both his wealth and wives one should protect his own self.

units.sanskrit: dyūtam etat purā kalpe dṛṣṭam vaira karam nṛṇām
units.english: From very olden times it hath been seen that gambling provoketh quarrels.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt dyūtam na seveta ha asya artham api buddhimān
units.english: Therefore, he that is wise, should not resort to it even in jest.

units.sanskrit: uktam mayā dyūta kāle api rājan
units.english: O son of Pratipa, at the time of that gambling match I told thee, O king--this is not proper.

units.sanskrit: na evam yuktam vacanam prātipīya tat auṣadham pathyam iva āturasya na rocate tava vaicitravīrya
units.english: But, O son of Vichitravirya, like medicine to a sick man, those words of mine were not agreeable to thee.

units.sanskrit: parājaiṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavān dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ
units.english: O king, thou desirest to vanquish the sons of Pandu, who are just as peacocks of variegated plumage, whereas thy sons are all as crows.

units.sanskrit: hitvā siṃhān kroṣṭukān gūhamānaḥ prāpte kāle śocitā tvam narendra
units.english: Forsaking lions thou art protecting jackals! O king, when the time cometh, thou wilt have to grieve for all this.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ tāta na krudhyati sarvakālam bhṛtyasya bhaktasya hite ratasya tasmin bhṛtyāḥ bhartari viśvasanti
units.english: That master, O sire, who doth not give vent to his displeasure with devoted servants zealously pursuing his good, enlisteth the confidence of his servants.

units.sanskrit: na ca enam āpatsu parityajanti
units.english: In fact, the latter adhere to him even in distress.

units.sanskrit: tyajanti hi enam ucita avaruddhāḥ snigdhāḥ hi amātyāḥ parihīna bhogāḥ
units.english: By confiscating the grants to one's servants or stopping their pay, one should not seek to amass wealth, for even affectionate counsellors deprived of their means of life and enjoyment, turn against him and leave him (in distress).

units.sanskrit: kṛtyāni pūrvam parisaṃkhyāya sarvāṇi āya vyayau anurūpām ca vṛttim saṃgṛhṇīyāt anurūpān sahāyān
units.english: Reflecting first on all intended acts and adjusting the wages and allowances of servants with his income and expenditure, a king should make proper alliances, for there is nothing that cannot be accomplished by alliances.

units.sanskrit: abhiprāyam yaḥ viditvā tu bhartuḥ sarvāṇi kāryāṇi karoti atandrīḥ vaktā hitānām anuraktaḥ āryaḥ
units.english: That officer who fully understanding the intentions of his royal master dischargeth all duties with alacrity, and who is respectable himself and devoted to his master, always telleth what is for his master's good, and who is fully acquainted with the extent of his own might and with that also of those against, whom he may be engaged, should be regarded by the king as his second self.

units.sanskrit: pratyāha yaḥ ca api niyujyamānaḥ prajñā abhimānī pratikūla vādī tyājyaḥ sa tādṛś tvarayā eva bhṛtyaḥ
units.english: That servant, however, who commanded (by his master) disregardeth the latter's injunctions and who enjoined to do anything refuseth to submit, proud as he is of his own intelligence and given to arguing against his master, should be got rid of without the least delay.

units.sanskrit: sa anukrośam ślakṣṇam a hāryam anyaiḥ aroga jātīyam udāra vākyam dūtam vadanti aṣṭaguṇa upapannam
units.english: Men of learning say that a servant should be endued with these eight qualities, viz., absence of pride, ability, absence of procrastination, kindness, cleanliness, incorruptibility, birth in a family free from the taint of disease, and weightiness of speech.

units.sanskrit: na viśvāsāt jātu parasya geham gacchet naraḥ cetayānaḥ vikāle
units.english: No man should confidently enter an enemy's house after dusk even with notice.

units.sanskrit: na catvare niśi tiṣṭhet nigūḍhaḥ na rājanyām yoṣitam prārthayīta na nihnavam satra gatasya gacchet
units.english: One should not at night lurk in the yard of another's premises, nor should one seek to enjoy a woman to whom the king himself might make love.

units.sanskrit: saṃsṛṣṭa mantrasya ku saṃgatasya
units.english: Never set thyself against the decision to which a person hath arrived who keepeth low company and who is in the habit of consulting all he meeteth.

units.sanskrit: na ca brūyāt na āśvasāmi tvayi iti sa kāraṇam vyapadeśam tu kuryāt
units.english: Never tell him,--I do not believe thee,--but assigning some reason send him away on a pretext.

units.sanskrit: putraḥ bhrātā vidhavā bāla putrā
units.english: A king who is exceedingly merciful, a woman of lewd character, the servant of a king, a son, a brother, a widow having an infant son one serving in the army, and one that hath suffered great losses, should never be engaged in pecuniary transactions of lending or borrowing.

units.sanskrit: senājīvī ca uddhṛta bhaktaḥ eva
units.english: When the king favours a person, that incident (of royal favour) bringeth in all others and holdeth them together.

units.sanskrit: guṇāḥ daśa snāna śīlam bhajante balam rūpam svara varṇa praśuddhiḥ sparśaḥ ca gandhaḥ ca viśuddha tā ca
units.english: He that performeth ablutions winneth these ten, viz., strength, beauty, a clear voice, capacity to utter all the alphabetical sounds, delicacy of touch, fineness of scent, cleanliness, gracefulness, delicacy of limbs, and beautiful women.

units.sanskrit: guṇāḥ ca ṣaṣ mita bhuktam bhajante ārogyam āyuḥ ca sukham balam ca
units.english: He that eateth sparingly winneth these six, viz., health, long life, and ease;

units.sanskrit: anāvilam ca asya bhavet apatyam na ca enam ādyūnaḥ iti kṣipanti
units.english: his progeny also becometh healthy, and nobody reproacheth him for gluttony.

units.sanskrit: loka dviṣṭam bahu māyam nṛśaṃsam a deśa kāla jñam aniṣṭa veṣam etān gṛhe na prativāsayīta
units.english: One should not give shelter to these in his house, viz., one that always acteth improperly, one that eateth too much, one that is hated by all, one that is exceedingly deceitful, one that is cruel, one that is ignorant of the proprieties of time and place, and one that dresseth indecently.

units.sanskrit: kadaryam ākrośakam aśrutam ca
units.english: A person, however distressed, should never solicit a miser for alms, or one that speaketh ill of others, or one that is unacquainted with the shastras, or a dweller in the woods, or one that is cunning, or one that doth not regard persons worthy of regard, or one that is cruel, or one that habitually quarrels with others, or one that is ungrateful.

units.sanskrit: nitya anṛtam ca adṛḍhabhaktikam ca vikṛṣṭa rāgam bahu māninam ca api etān na seveta nara adhamān ṣaṭ
units.english: A person should never wait upon these six worst of men, viz., one that is a foe, one that always errs, one that is wedded to falsehood, one that is wanting in devotion to the gods, one that is without affection, and one that always regards himself competent to do everything.

units.sanskrit: sahāya bandhanāḥ hi arthāḥ sahāyāḥ ca artha bandhanāḥ
units.english: One's purposes depend (for their success) on means;

units.sanskrit: anyonya bandhanau etau vinā anyonyam na sidhyataḥ
units.english: They are intimately connected with each other, so that success depends on both.

units.sanskrit: vṛttim ca tebhyaḥ anuvidhāya kām cit sthāne kumārīḥ pratipādya sarvā araṇya saṃsthaḥ muni vat bubhūṣet
units.english: Begetting sons and rendering them independent by making some provision for them, and bestowing maiden daughters on eligible persons, one should retire to the woods, and desire to live as a Muni.

units.sanskrit: hitam yat sarva bhūtānām ātmanaḥ ca sukha āvaham tat kuryāt īśvaraḥ hi etat mūlam dharma artha siddhaye
units.english: One should, for obtaining the favours of the Supreme Being, do that which is for the good of all creatures as also for his own happiness, for it is this which is the root of the successful of all one's objects.

units.sanskrit: vyavasāyaḥ ca yasya syāt tasya avṛtti bhayam kutas paśya doṣān pāṇḍavaiḥ vigrahe tvam yatra vyatheran api devāḥ sa śakrāḥ
units.english: What anxiety hath he for a livelihood that hath intelligence, energy, prowess, strength, alacrity and perseverance? 'Behold the evils of a rupture with the Pandavas which would sadden the very gods with Sakra.

units.sanskrit: putraiḥ vairam nityam udvigna vāso
units.english: These are, first, enmity between them that are all thy sons;

units.sanskrit: yaśaḥ praṇāśaḥ dviṣatām ca harṣaḥ
units.english: and lastly, the joy of those that are thy enemies.

units.sanskrit: bhīṣmasya kopaḥ tava ca indra kalpa droṇasya rājñaḥ ca yudhiṣṭhirasya utsādayet lokam imam pravṛddhaḥ
units.english: The wrath of Bhishma, O thou of the splendour of Indra, of Drona, and the king Yudhishthira, will consume the whole world, like a comet of large proportions falling transversely on the earth.

units.sanskrit: tava putra śatam ca eva karṇaḥ pañca ca pāṇḍavāḥ pṛthivīm anuśāseyuḥ akhilām sāgara ambarām
units.english: Thy hundred sons and Karna and the sons of Pandu can together rule the vast earth with the belt of the seas.

units.sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ vanam rājan vyāghrāḥ pāṇḍu sutāḥ matāḥ
units.english: O king, the Dhartarashtras constitute a forest of which the Pandavas are, I think, tigers.

units.sanskrit: mā vanam chindhi sa vyāghram mā vyāghrāt nīnaśaḥ vanāt na syāt vanam ṛte vyāghrān vyāghrāḥ na syuḥ ṛte vanam
units.english: O, do not cut down that forest with its tigers! O, let not the tigers be driven from that forest! There can be no forest without tigers, and no tigers without a forest.

units.sanskrit: vanam hi rakṣyate vyāghraiḥ vyāghrān rakṣati kānanam na tathā icchanti akalyāṇāḥ pareṣām veditum guṇān yathā eṣām jñātum icchanti nairguṇyam pāpa cetasaḥ
units.english: The forest shelters the tigers and tigers guard the forest!' They that are sinful never seek so much to ascertain the good qualities of others as to ascertain their faults.

units.sanskrit: artha siddhim parām icchan dharmam eva āditas caret na hi dharmāt apaiti arthaḥ svarga lokāt iva amṛtam
units.english: He that desires the highest success in all matters connected with worldly profit, should from the very beginning practise virtue, for true profit is never separated from heaven.

units.sanskrit: yasya ātmā virataḥ pāpāt kalyāṇe ca niveśitaḥ
units.english: He whose soul hath been dissociated from sin and firmly fixed on virtue, hath understood all things in their natural and adventitious states;

units.sanskrit: yaḥ dharmam artham kāmam ca yathākālam niṣevate dharma artha kāma saṃyogam saḥ amutra iha ca vindati
units.english: he that followeth virtue, profit, and desire, in proper seasons, obtaineth, both here and hereafter, a combination of all three.

units.sanskrit: saṃniyacchati yaḥ vegam utthitam krodha harṣayoḥ sa śriyaḥ bhājanam rājan yaḥ ca āpatsu na muhyati
units.english: He that restraineth the force of both anger and joy, and never, O king, loseth his senses under calamities, winneth prosperity.

units.sanskrit: balam pañcavidham nityam puruṣāṇām nibodha me
units.english: Listen to me, O king. Men are said to have five different kinds of strength, Of these, the strength of arms is regarded to be of the most inferior kind.

units.sanskrit: amātya lābhaḥ bhadram te dvitīyam balam ucyate
units.english: Blessed be thou, the acquisition of good counsellors is regarded as the second kind of strength.

units.sanskrit: dhana lābhaḥ tṛtīyam tu balam āhuḥ jigīṣavaḥ
units.english: The wise have said that the acquisition of wealth is the third kind of strength.

units.sanskrit: yat tu asya sahajam rājan pitṛpaitāmaham balam abhijātabalam nāma tat caturtham balam smṛtam
units.english: The strength of birth, O king, which one naturally acquireth from one's sires and grandsires, is regarded as the fourth kind of strength.

units.sanskrit: yena tu etāni sarvāṇi saṃgṛhītāni bhārata yat balānām balam śreṣṭham tat prajñābalam ucyate
units.english: That, however, O Bharata, by which all these are won, and which is the foremost of all kinds of strength, is called the strength of the intellect.

units.sanskrit: mahate yaḥ apakārāya narasya prabhavet naraḥ tena vairam samāsajya dūra sthaḥ asmi iti na āśvaset
units.english: Having provoked the hostility of a person who is capable of inflicting great injury on a fellow creature, one should not gather assurance from the thought that one liveth at a distance from the other.

units.sanskrit: strīṣu rājasu sarpeṣu svādhyāye śatru seviṣu bhoge ca āyuṣi viśvāsam kaḥ prājñaḥ kartum arhati prajñā śareṇa abhihatasya jantoḥ
units.english: Who that is wise that can place his trust on women, kings, serpents, his own master, enemies, enjoyments, and period of life? There are no physicians nor medicines for one that hath been struck by the arrow of wisdom.

units.sanskrit: na homa mantrāḥ na ca maṅgalāni na ātharvaṇāḥ na api agadāḥ su siddhāḥ
units.english: In the case of such a person neither the mantras of homa, nor auspicious ceremonies, nor the mantras of the Atharva Veda, nor any of the antidotes of poison, are of any efficacy.

units.sanskrit: sarpaḥ ca agniḥ ca siṃhaḥ ca kula putraḥ ca bhārata na avajñeyāḥ manuṣyeṇa sarve te hi atitejasaḥ
units.english: Serpents, fire, lions, and consanguineous relatives,--none of these, O Bharata, should be disregarded by a man; all of these are possessed of great power.

units.sanskrit: agniḥ tejaḥ mahat loke gūḍhaḥ tiṣṭhati dāruṣu
units.english: Fire is a thing of great energy in this world.

units.sanskrit: na ca upayuṅkte tat dāru yāvat naḥ dīpyate paraiḥ
units.english: It lurketh in wood and never consumeth it till it is ignited by others.

units.sanskrit: saḥ eva khalu dārubhyaḥ yadā nirmathya dīpyate tadā tat ca vanam ca anyat nirdahati āśu tejasā
units.english: That very fire, when brought out by friction, consumeth by its energy not only the wood in which it lurketh, but also an entire forest and many other things.

units.sanskrit: evam eva kule jātāḥ pāvaka upama tejasaḥ
units.english: Men of high lineage are just like fire in energy.

units.sanskrit: kṣamāvantaḥ nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe agniḥ iva śerate
units.english: Endued with forgiveness, they betray no outward symptoms of wrath and are quiet like fire in wood.

units.sanskrit: latā dharmā tvam sa putraḥ śālāḥ pāṇḍu sutāḥ matāḥ
units.english: Thou, O king, with thy sons art possessed of the virtue of creepers, and the sons of Pandu are regarded as Sala trees.

units.sanskrit: na latā vardhate jātu mahā drumam an āśritā
units.english: A creeper never groweth unless there is a large tree to twine round.

units.sanskrit: vanam rājan tvam sa putraḥ ambikeya
units.english: O king, O son of Ambika, thy son is as a forest.

units.sanskrit: siṃhān vane pāṇḍavān tāta viddhi
units.english: O sire, know that the Pandavas are the lions of that forest.

units.sanskrit: siṃhāḥ vinaśyeyuḥ ṛte vanena viduraḥ uvāca ūrdhvam prāṇāḥ hi utkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthaviraḥ āyati
units.english: Without its lions the forest is doomed to destruction, and lions also are doomed to destruction without the forest (to shelter them).'" SECTION XXXVIII "Vidura said, 'The heart of a young man, when an aged and venerable person cometh to his house (as a guest), soareth aloft.

units.sanskrit: pratyutthāna abhivādābhyām punar tān pratipadyate pīṭham dattvā sādhave abhyāgatāya
units.english: By advancing forward and saluting him, he getteth it back.

units.sanskrit: ānīya apaḥ parinirṇijya pādau sukham pṛṣṭvā prativedya ātma saṃstham tatas dadyāt annam avekṣya dhīraḥ
units.english: He that is self-controlled, first offering a seat, and bringing water and causing his guest's feet to be washed and making the usual enquiries of welcome, should then speak of his own affairs, and taking everything into consideration, offer him food.

units.sanskrit: yasya udakam madhuparkam ca gām ca na mantra vid pratigṛhṇāti gehe lobhāt bhayāt artha kārpaṇyataḥ vā
units.english: The wise have said that man liveth in vain in whose dwelling a Brahmana conversant with mantras doth not accept water, honey and curds, and kine from fear of being unable to appropriate them, or from miserliness and unwillingness with which the gifts are made.

units.sanskrit: senājīvī śrutivikrāyakaḥ ca bhṛśam priyaḥ api atithiḥ na udaka arhaḥ
units.english: A physician, a maker of arrows, even one that hath given up the vow of Brahmacharya before it is complete, a thief, a crooked-minded man, a Brahmana that drinks, one that causeth miscarriage, one that liveth by serving in the army, and one that selleth the Vedas, when arrived as a guest, however undeserving he may be the offer of water should be regarded (by a householder) as exceedingly dear.

units.sanskrit: dadhi kṣīram madhu tailam ghṛtam ca tilāḥ māṃsam mūla phalāni śākam raktam vāsaḥ sarvagandhāḥ guḍaḥ ca
units.english: A Brahmana should never be a seller of salt, of cooked food, curds, milk, honey, oil, clarified butter, sesame, meat, fruits, roots, potherbs, dyed clothes, all kinds of perfumery, and treacle.

units.sanskrit: prahīṇa śokaḥ gata saṃdhi vigrahaḥ nindā praśaṃsā uparataḥ priya apriye caran udāsīna vat eṣa bhikṣukaḥ
units.english: He that never giveth way to anger, he that is above grief, he that is no longer in need of friendship and quarrels, he that disregardeth both praise and blame, and he that standeth aloof from both what is agreeable and disagreeable, like one perfectly withdrawn from the world, is a real Yogin of the Bhikshu order.

units.sanskrit: su saṃyata ātma agni kāryeṣu a codyaḥ vane vasan atithiṣu apramattaḥ dhuraṃdharaḥ puṇya kṛt eṣa tāpasaḥ
units.english: That virtuous ascetic who liveth on rice growing wild, or roots, or potherbs, who hath his soul under control, who carefully keepeth his fire for worship, and dwelling in the woods is always regardful of guests, is indeed, the foremost of his brotherhood.

units.sanskrit: apakṛtvā buddhimataḥ dūra sthaḥ asmi iti na āśvaset
units.english: Having wronged an intelligent person, one should never gather assurance from the fact that one liveth at a distance from the person wronged.

units.sanskrit: dīrghau buddhimataḥ bāhū yābhyām hiṃsati hiṃsitaḥ na viśvaset aviśvaste viśvaste na ativiśvaset viśvāsāt bhayam utpannam mūlāni api nikṛntati
units.english: Long are the arms which intelligent persons have, by which they can return wrongs for wrongs done to them, One should never put trust on him who should not be trusted, nor put too much trust on him who should be trusted, for the danger that ariseth from one's having reposed trust on another cutteth off one's very roots.

units.sanskrit: anīrṣyuḥ gupta dāraḥ syāt saṃvibhāgī priyaṃvadaḥ
units.english: One should renounce envy, protect one's wives, give to others what is their due, and be agreeable in speech.

units.sanskrit: ślakṣṇaḥ madhura vāc strīṇām na ca āsām vaśa gaḥ bhavet
units.english: One should be sweet-tongued and pleasant in his address as regards one's wives, but should never be their slave.

units.sanskrit: pūjanīyāḥ mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāḥ ca gṛha dīptayaḥ striyaḥ śriyaḥ gṛhasya uktāḥ tasmāt rakṣyāḥ viśeṣataḥ
units.english: It hath been said that wives that are highly blessed and virtuous, worthy of worship and the ornaments of their homes, are really embodiments of domestic prosperity. They should, therefore, be protected particularly.

units.sanskrit: pituḥ antaḥpuram dadyāt mātuḥ dadyāt mahānasam
units.english: One should devolve the looking over of his inner apartments on his father; of the kitchen, on his mother;

units.sanskrit: goṣu ca ātma samam dadyāt svayam eva kṛṣim vrajet
units.english: of the kine, on somebody he looks upon as his own self, but as regards agriculture, one should look over it himself.

units.sanskrit: bhṛtyaiḥ vaṇijya ācāram ca putraiḥ seveta brāhmaṇān
units.english: One should look after guests of the trader-caste through his servants, and those of the Brahmana caste through his sons.

units.sanskrit: adbhyaḥ agniḥ brahmataḥ kṣatram aśmanaḥ loham utthitam
units.english: Fire hath its origin in water; Kshatriyas in Brahmanas; and iron in stone.

units.sanskrit: teṣām sarvatragam tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
units.english: The energy of those (i.e., fire, Kshatriyas, and iron) can affect all things but is neutralised as soon as the things come in contact with their progenitors.

units.sanskrit: kṣamāvantaḥ nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe agniḥ iva śerate
units.english: Fire lieth concealed in wood without showing itself externally.

units.sanskrit: yasya mantram na jānanti bāhyāḥ ca abhyantarāḥ ca ye sa rājā sarvatas cakṣuḥ ciram aiśvaryam aśnute
units.english: That king whose counsels cannot be known by either outsiders or those about him, but who knoweth the counsels of others through his spies, enjoyeth his prosperity long.

units.sanskrit: kariṣyan na prabhāṣeta kṛtāni eva ca darśayet
units.english: One should never speak of what one intends to do.

units.sanskrit: dharma kāma artha kāryāṇi tathā mantraḥ na bhidyate
units.english: Let anything thou doest in respect of virtue, profit, and desire, be not known till it is done.

units.sanskrit: giri pṛṣṭham upāruhya prāsādam vā rahaḥ gataḥ araṇye niḥśalāke vā tatra mantraḥ vidhīyate
units.english: Ascending on the mountain-top or on the terrace of a palace, or proceeding to a wilderness devoid of trees and plants, one should, in secrecy, mature his counsels.

units.sanskrit: na a suhṛd paramam mantram bhārata arhati veditum apaṇḍitaḥ vā api suhṛd paṇḍitaḥ vā api anātmavān
units.english: O Bharata, neither a friend who is without learning, nor a learned friend who hath no control over his senses, deserveth to be a repository of state secrets.

units.sanskrit: na a parīkṣya mahīpālaḥ kuryāt sacivam ātmanaḥ amātye hi artha lipsā ca mantra rakṣaṇam eva ca
units.english: O king, never make one thy minister without examining him well, for a king's finances and the keeping of his counsels both depend on his minister.

units.sanskrit: kṛtāni sarva kāryāṇi yasya vā pārṣadāḥ viduḥ dharme ca arthe ca kāme ca sa rājā rāja sattamaḥ
units.english: That king is the foremost of rulers, whose ministers know his acts in respect of virtue, profit and desire, only after they are done.

units.sanskrit: gūḍha mantrasya nṛpateḥ tasya siddhiḥ asaṃśayam
units.english: The king whose counsels are kept close, without doubt, commandeth success.

units.sanskrit: apraśastāni karmāṇi yaḥ mohāt anutiṣṭhati sa teṣām viparibhraṃśe bhraśyate jīvitāt api
units.english: He that from ignorance committeth acts that are censurable, loseth his very life in consequence of the untoward results of those acts.

units.sanskrit: karmaṇām tu praśastānām anuṣṭhānam sukha āvaham
units.english: The doing of acts that are praise-worthy is always attended with ease.

units.sanskrit: teṣām eva ananuṣṭhānam paścāttāpa karam mahat
units.english: Omission to do such acts leadeth to repentance.

units.sanskrit: an adhītya yathā vedān na vipraḥ śrāddham arhati evam a śruta ṣāḍguṇyaḥ na mantram śrotum arhati
units.english: As a Brahmana without having studied the Vedas is not fit to officiate at a Sraddha (in honour of the Pitris), so he that hath not heard of the six (means for protecting a kingdom) deserveth not to take part in political deliberations.

units.sanskrit: sthāna vṛddhi kṣaya jñasya ṣāḍguṇya vidita ātmanaḥ an avajñāta śīlasya svādhīnā pṛthivī nṛpa
units.english: O king, he that hath an eye upon increase, decrease, and surplus, he that is conversant with the six means and knoweth also his own self, he whose conduct is always applauded, bringeth the whole earth under subjection to himself.

units.sanskrit: amogha krodha harṣasya svayam kṛtyā anvavekṣiṇaḥ ātma pratyaya kośasya vasudhā iyam vasuṃdharā
units.english: He whose anger and joy are productive of consequences, he who looketh over personally what should be done, he who hath his treasury under his own control, bringeth the whole earth under subjection to himself.

units.sanskrit: nāma mātreṇa tuṣyeta chatreṇa ca mahīpatiḥ
units.english: The king should be content with the name he wins and the umbrella that is held over his head.

units.sanskrit: bhṛtyebhyaḥ visṛjet arthān na ekaḥ sarva haraḥ bhavet
units.english: Alone he should not appropriate everything.

units.sanskrit: brāhmaṇaḥ brāhmaṇam veda bhartā veda striyam tathā amātyam nṛpatiḥ veda rājā rājānam eva ca
units.english: A Brahmana knoweth a Brahmana, the husband understandeth the wife, the king knoweth the minister, and monarchs know monarchs.

units.sanskrit: na śatruḥ aṅkam āpannaḥ moktavyaḥ vadhya tām gataḥ
units.english: A foe that deserveth death, when brought under subjection should never be set free.

units.sanskrit: nyak bhūtvā paryupāsīta vadhyam hanyāt bale sati
units.english: If one be weak one should pay court to one's foe that is stronger, even if the latter deserves death;

units.sanskrit: a hanyamānaḥ bhaya kṛt na hatāt jāyate bhayam
units.english: but one should kill that foe as soon as one commandeth sufficient strength, for, if not killed, dangers soon arise from him.

units.sanskrit: daivateṣu ca yatnena rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca niyantavyaḥ sadā krodhaḥ vṛddha bāla ātureṣu ca
units.english: One should, with an effort, control his wrath against the gods, kings, Brahmanas, old men, children, and those that are helpless.

units.sanskrit: nirartham kalaham prājñaḥ varjayet mūḍha sevitam
units.english: He that is wise should avoid unprofitable quarrels such as fools only engage in.

units.sanskrit: kīrtim ca labhate loke na ca anarthena yujyate
units.english: By this one winneth great fame in this world and avoideth misery and unhappiness.

units.sanskrit: prasādaḥ niṣphalaḥ yasya krodhaḥ ca api nirarthakaḥ na tam bhartāram icchanti ṣaṇḍham patim iva striyaḥ
units.english: People never desire him for a master whose grace is fruitless and whose wrath goest for nothing, like women never desiring him for a husband who is a eunuch.

units.sanskrit: na buddhiḥ dhana lābhāya na jāḍyam asamṛddhaye
units.english: Intelligence doth not exist for the acquisition of wealth, nor is idleness the cause of adversity;

units.sanskrit: loka paryāya vṛttāntam prājñaḥ jānāti na itaraḥ
units.english: the man of wisdom only knoweth, and not others, the cause of the diversities of condition in this world.

units.sanskrit: vidyā śīla vayaḥ vṛddhān buddhi vṛddhān ca bhārata dhana abhijana vṛddhān ca nityam mūḍhaḥ avamanyate
units.english: The fool, O Bharata, always disregardeth those that are elderly in years, and eminent in conduct and knowledge, in intelligence, wealth, and lineage.

units.sanskrit: anārya vṛttam aprājñam asūyakam adhārmikam anarthāḥ kṣipram āyānti vāc duṣṭam krodhanam tathā
units.english: Calamities soon come upon them that are of wicked disposition, devoid of wisdom, envious, or sinful, foul-tongued, and wrathful.

units.sanskrit: avisaṃvādanam dānam samayasya avyatikramaḥ āvartayanti bhūtāni samyak praṇihitā ca vāc
units.english: Absence of deceitfulness, gift, observance of the established rules of intercourse, and speech well-controlled, bring all creatures under subjection.

units.sanskrit: avisaṃvādakaḥ dakṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ matimān ṛjuḥ api saṃkṣīṇa kośaḥ api labhate parivāraṇam
units.english: He that is without deceitfulness, he that is active, grateful, intelligent, and guileless, even if his treasury be empty, obtaineth friends, counsellors, and servants.

units.sanskrit: dhṛtiḥ śamaḥ damaḥ śaucam kāruṇyam vāc aniṣṭhurā mitrāṇām ca anabhidrohaḥ sapta etāḥ samidhaḥ śriyaḥ
units.english: Intelligence, tranquillity of mind, self-control, purity, absence of harsh speech and unwillingness to do anything disagreeable to friends,--these seven are regarded as the fuel of prosperity's flame.

units.sanskrit: asaṃvibhāgī duṣṭa ātmā kṛtaghnaḥ nirapatrapaḥ tādṛś nara adhamaḥ loke varjanīyaḥ nara adhipa
units.english: The wretch who doth not give to others their due, who is of wicked soul, who is ungrateful, and shameless, should, O king, be avoided.

units.sanskrit: na sa rātrau sukham śete sa sarpaḥ iva veśmani yaḥ kopayati nirdoṣam sa doṣaḥ abhyantaram janam
units.english: The guilty person who provoketh another about him that is innocent, cannot sleep peacefully at night, like a person passing the night with a snake in the same room.

units.sanskrit: yeṣu duṣṭeṣu doṣaḥ syāt yogakṣemasya bhārata sadā prasādanam teṣām devatānām iva ācaret
units.english: They, O Bharata, who upon being angry endanger one's possessions and means of acquisition, should always be propitiated like the very gods.

units.sanskrit: ye arthāḥ strīṣu samāsaktāḥ prathama utpatiteṣu ca
units.english: Those objects that depend upon women, careless persons, men that have fallen away from the duties of their caste, and those that are wicked in disposition, are doubtful of success.

units.sanskrit: ye ca anārya samāsaktāḥ sarve te saṃśayam gatāḥ
units.english: They sink helplessly.

units.sanskrit: yatra strī yatra kitavaḥ yatra bālaḥ anuśāsti ca majjanti te avaśāḥ deśāḥ nadyām aśma plavāḥ iva
units.english: O king, like a raft made of stone, who have a woman, a deceitful person, or a child, for their guide.

units.sanskrit: yam praśaṃsanti kitavāḥ yam praśaṃsanti cāraṇāḥ yam praśaṃsanti bandhakyaḥ na sa jīvati mānavaḥ hitvā tān parama iṣvāsān pāṇḍavān amita ojasaḥ
units.english: They that are competent in the general principles of work, though not in particular kinds of work are regarded by men as learned and wise for particular kinds of work, are subsidiary, That man who is highly spoken of by swindlers, mimes and women of ill fame, is more dead than alive, Forsaking these mighty bowmen of immeasurable energy, viz., the son of Pandu, thou hast.

units.sanskrit: āhitam bhārata aiśvaryam tvayā duryodhane mahat
units.english: O Bharata, devolved on Duryodhana, the cares of a mighty empire.

units.sanskrit: tam drakṣyasi paribhraṣṭam tasmāt tvam nacirāt iva aiśvarya mada saṃmūḍham balim lokatrayāt iva dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca
units.english: Thou shalt, therefore, soon see that swelling affluence fall off, like Vali fallen off from the three worlds.'" SECTION XXXIX "Dhritarashtra said, 'Man is not the disposer of either his prosperity or adversity.

units.sanskrit: sūtra protā dāru mayī iva yoṣā
units.english: He is like a wooden doll moved by strings.

units.sanskrit: dhātrā tu diṣṭasya vaśe kila ayam
units.english: Indeed, the Creator hath made man subject to Destiny.

units.sanskrit: viduraḥ uvāca a prāpta kālam vacanam bṛhaspatiḥ api bruvan labhate buddhi avajñānam avamānam ca bhārata
units.english: Go on telling me, I am attentive to what thou sayest.' "Vidura said, 'O Bharata, by speaking words out of season even Vrihaspati himself incurreth reproach and the charge of ignorance, one becometh agreeable by gift, another by sweet words, a third by the force of incantation and drugs.

units.sanskrit: priyaḥ bhavati dānena priya vādena ca aparaḥ
units.english: He, however, that is naturally agreeable, always remaineth so.

units.sanskrit: dveṣyaḥ na sādhuḥ bhavati na medhāvī na paṇḍitaḥ
units.english: He that is hated by another is never regarded by that other as honest or intelligent or wise.

units.sanskrit: priye śubhāni karmāṇi dveṣye pāpāni bhārata
units.english: One attributeth everything good to him one loveth;

units.sanskrit: duryodhanam tyaja putram tvam ekam tasya tyāgāt putra śatasya vṛddhiḥ asya atyāgāt putra śatasya nāśaḥ
units.english: O king, as soon as Duryodhana was born I told thee,--thou shouldst abandon this one son, for by abandoning him thou wouldst secure the prosperity of thy hundred sons,--and by keeping him, destruction would overtake thy hundred sons, that gain should never be regarded highly which leadeth to loss.

units.sanskrit: kṣayaḥ api bahu mantavyaḥ yaḥ kṣayaḥ vṛddhim āvahet
units.english: On the other hand, that loss even should be regarded highly which would bring on gain.

units.sanskrit: na sa kṣayaḥ mahā rāja yaḥ kṣayaḥ vṛddhim āvahet
units.english: That is no loss, O king, which bringeth on gain.

units.sanskrit: kṣayaḥ sa tu iha mantavyaḥ yam labdhvā bahu nāśayet
units.english: That, however, should be reckoned as loss which is certain to bring about greater losses still.

units.sanskrit: samṛddhāḥ guṇataḥ ke cid bhavanti dhanataḥ apare
units.english: Some become eminent in consequence of good qualities; others become so in consequence of wealth.

units.sanskrit: dhana vṛddhān guṇaiḥ hīnān dhṛtarāṣṭra vivarjayet dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca sarvam tvam āyatī yuktam bhāṣase prājña saṃmatam
units.english: Avoid them, O Dhritarashtra, that are eminent in wealth but destitute of good qualities!' "Dhritarashtra said, 'All that you sayest is approved by the wise and is for my future good.

units.sanskrit: na ca utsahe sutam tyaktum yatas dharmaḥ tatas jayaḥ
units.english: I dare not, however, abandon my son.

units.sanskrit: viduraḥ uvāca svabhāva guṇa saṃpannaḥ na jātu vinaya anvitaḥ
units.english: It is well-known that where there is righteousness there is victory.' "Vidura said, 'He that is graced with every virtue and is endued with humility, is never indifferent to even the minutest sufferings of living creatures.

units.sanskrit: para apavāda niratāḥ para duḥkha udayeṣu ca paraspara virodhe ca yatante satata utthitāḥ
units.english: They, however, that are ever employed in speaking ill of others, always strive with activity quarrelling with one another and in all matters, calculated to give pain to others.

units.sanskrit: sa doṣam darśanam yeṣām saṃvāse su mahat bhayam artha ādāne mahān doṣaḥ pradāne ca mahat bhayam
units.english: There is sin in accepting gifts from, and danger in making gifts to them, whose very sight is inauspicious and whose companionship is fraught with danger.

units.sanskrit: ye vai bhedana śīlāḥ tu sa kāmāḥ nistrapāḥ śaṭhāḥ ye pāpāḥ iti vikhyātāḥ saṃvāse parigarhitāḥ
units.english: They that are quarrelsome, covetous, shameless, deceitful, are known unrighteous, and their companionship should always be avoided.

units.sanskrit: yuktāḥ ca anyaiḥ mahā doṣaiḥ ye narāḥ tān vivarjayet nivartamāne sauhārde prītiḥ nīce praṇaśyati yā ca eva phala nirvṛttiḥ sauhṛde ca eva yat sukham
units.english: One should also avoid those men that are endued with similar faults of a grave nature, When the occasion that caused the friendship is over the friendship of those that are low, the beneficial result of that connection, and the happiness also derivable from it, all come to an end.

units.sanskrit: alpe api apakṛte mohāt na śāntim upagacchati
units.english: They then strive to speak ill of their (late) friend and endeavour to inflict loss on him, and if the loss they sustain be even very small, for all that they, from want of self-control, fail to enjoy peace.

units.sanskrit: tādṛśaiḥ saṃgatam nīcaiḥ nṛśaṃsaiḥ akṛtātmabhiḥ niśāmya nipuṇam buddhyā vidvān dūrāt vivarjayet
units.english: He that is learned, examining everything carefully and reflecting well, should, from a distance, avoid the friendship of vile and wicked-minded persons such as these.

units.sanskrit: yaḥ jñātim anugṛhṇāti daridram dīnam āturam sa putra paśubhiḥ vṛddhim yaśaḥ ca avyayam aśnute
units.english: He that helpeth his poor and wretched and helpless relatives, obtain children and animals and enjoyeth prosperity that knoweth no end.

units.sanskrit: jñātayaḥ vardhanīyāḥ taiḥ ye icchanti ātmanaḥ śubham
units.english: They that desire their own benefit should always succour their relatives.

units.sanskrit: kula vṛddhim ca rāja indra tasmāt sādhu samācara
units.english: By every means, therefore, O king, do thou seek the growth of thy race.

units.sanskrit: śreyasā yokṣyase rājan kurvāṇaḥ jñāti satkriyām
units.english: Prosperity will be thine, O Monarch, if thou behavest well towards all thy relatives.

units.sanskrit: viguṇāḥ hi api saṃrakṣyāḥ jñātayaḥ bharata ṛṣabha
units.english: Even relatives that are destitute of good qualities should be protected.

units.sanskrit: kim punar guṇavantaḥ te tvad prasāda abhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ prasādam kuru dīnānām pāṇḍavānām viśām pate dīyantām grāmakāḥ ke cid teṣām vṛtti artham īśvara
units.english: O bull of the Bharata race, how much more, therefore, should they be protected that are endued with every virtue and are humbly expectant of thy favours? Favour thou the heroic sons of Pandu, O monarch, and let a few villages be assigned to them for their maintenance.

units.sanskrit: evam loke yaśaḥ prāptaḥ bhaviṣyasi narādhipa
units.english: By acting thus, O king, fame will be thine in this world.

units.sanskrit: vṛddhena hi tvayā kāryam putrāṇām tāta rakṣaṇam
units.english: Thou art old; thou shouldst, therefore, control thy sons.

units.sanskrit: mayā ca api hitam vācyam viddhi mām tvad hita eṣiṇam
units.english: I should say what is for thy good. Know me as one that wishes well to thee.

units.sanskrit: jñātibhiḥ vigrahaḥ tāta na kartavyaḥ bhava arthinā sukhāni saha bhojyāni jñātibhiḥ bharata ṛṣabha saṃbhojanam saṃkathanam saṃprītiḥ ca parasparam
units.english: O bull of the Bharata race, happiness should ever be enjoyed with one's relatives, and not without them, to eat with one another, to talk with one another, and to love one another, are what relatives should always do.

units.sanskrit: jñātibhiḥ saha kāryāṇi na virodhaḥ katham cana
units.english: They should never quarrel.

units.sanskrit: jñātayaḥ tārayanti iha jñātayaḥ majjayanti ca
units.english: In this world it is the relatives that rescue, and the relatives that ruin (relatives).

units.sanskrit: su vṛttāḥ tārayanti iha durvṛttāḥ majjayanti ca
units.english: while those that are unrighteous sink (their brethren).

units.sanskrit: su vṛttaḥ bhava rāja indra pāṇḍavān prati mānada
units.english: O king, be thou, O giver of honours, righteous in thy conduct towards the sons of Pandu.

units.sanskrit: a dharṣaṇīyaḥ śatrūṇām taiḥ vṛtaḥ tvam bhaviṣyasi
units.english: Surrounded by them, thou wouldst be unconquerable by thy foes.

units.sanskrit: sīdatā yat kṛtam tena tat pāpam samam aśnute digdha hastam mṛgaḥ iva saḥ enaḥ tasya vindati
units.english: If a relative shrinks in the presence of a prosperous relative, like a deer at sight of a hunter armed with arrows, then the prosperous relative hath to take upon himself all the sins of the other.

units.sanskrit: paścāt api nara śreṣṭha tava tāpaḥ bhaviṣyati tān vā hatān sutān vā api śrutvā tat anucintaya
units.english: O best of men, repentance will be thine (for this thy inaction at present) when in future thou wilt hear of the death of either the Pandavas or thy sons.

units.sanskrit: yena khaṭvām samārūḍhaḥ paritapyeta karmaṇā ādau eva na tat kuryāt adhruve jīvite sati
units.english: When life itself is unstable, one should in the very beginning avoid that act in consequence of which one would have to indulge in regrets having entered the chamber of woe.

units.sanskrit: na kaḥ cit na apanayate pumān anyatra bhārgavāt
units.english: True it is that a person other than Bhargava, the author of the science of morality is liable to commit actions that go against morality.

units.sanskrit: śeṣa saṃpratipattiḥ tu buddhimatsu eva tiṣṭhati
units.english: It is seen, however, that a just notion of consequence is present in all persons of intelligence.

units.sanskrit: duryodhanena yadi etat pāpam teṣu purā kṛtam
units.english: If Duryodhana inflicted these wrongs on the sons of Pandu, it is thy duty, O king of men, to undo them all.

units.sanskrit: tvayā tat kula vṛddhena pratyāneyam nareśvara tān tvam pade pratiṣṭhāpya loke vigata kalmaṣaḥ bhaviṣyasi nara śreṣṭha pūjanīyaḥ manīṣiṇām
units.english: Re-instating them in their position, thou wilt, in this world, be cleansed of all thy sins and be, O king of men, an object of worship with even those that have their souls under control.

units.sanskrit: su vyāhṛtāni dhīrāṇām phalataḥ pravicintya yaḥ adhyavasyati kāryeṣu ciram yaśasi tiṣṭhati
units.english: Reflecting on the well-spoken words of the wise according to their consequences, he that engageth in acts never loseth fame.

units.sanskrit: asamyak upayuktam hi jñānam su kuśalaiḥ api upalabhya api aviditam viditam ca api anuṣṭhitam
units.english: The knowledge imparted by even men of learning and skill is imperfect, for that which is sought to be inculcated is ill-understood, or, if understood, is not accomplished in practice.

units.sanskrit: pāpa udaya phalam vidvān yaḥ na ārabhati vardhate
units.english: That learned person who never doth an act, the consequences of which are sin and misery, always groweth (in prosperity).

units.sanskrit: yaḥ tu pūrva kṛtam pāpam a vimṛśya anuvartate saḥ anya aparādhe durmedhāḥ viṣame vinipātyate
units.english: The person, however, of wicked soul, who from folly pursueth his sinful course commenced before falleth into a slough of deep mire.

units.sanskrit: mantrabhedasya ṣaṭ prājñaḥ dvārāṇi imāni lakṣayet artha saṃtati kāmaḥ ca rakṣet etāni nityaśas
units.english: He that is wise should ever keep in view the (following) six conduits by which counsels become divulged, and he that desireth success and a long dynasty should ever guard himself from those six.

units.sanskrit: madam svapnam avijñānam ākāram ca ātma saṃbhavam duṣṭa amātyeṣu viśrambham dūtāt ca akuśalāt api
units.english: They are, intoxication, sleep, inattention to spies, set over one by another, one's own demeanour as dependent on the working of one's own heart, confidence reposed on a wicked counsellor, and unskilful envoys.

units.sanskrit: dvārāṇi etāni yaḥ jñātvā saṃvṛṇoti sadā nṛpaḥ trivarga caraṇe yuktaḥ sa śatrūn adhitiṣṭhati
units.english: Knowing these six doors (through which counsels are divulged), he that keepeth them shut while pursuing the attainment of virtue, profit, and desire, succeedeth in standing over the heads of his foes.

units.sanskrit: na vai śrutam a vijñāya vṛddhān an upasevya ca dharma arthau veditum śakyau bṛhaspati samaiḥ api
units.english: Without an acquaintance with the scriptures and without waiting upon the old, neither virtue nor profit can be known (or won) by persons blessed even with the intelligence of Vrihaspati.

units.sanskrit: naṣṭam samudre patitam naṣṭam vākyam a śṛṇvati
units.english: A thing is lost if cast into the sea; words are lost if addressed to one that listens not;

units.sanskrit: anātmani śrutam naṣṭam naṣṭam śrutam anagnikam
units.english: the scriptures are lost on one that hath not his soul under control;

units.sanskrit: matyā parīkṣya medhāvī buddhyā saṃpādya ca asakṛt śrutvā dṛṣṭvā atha vijñāya prājñaḥ mantram samācaret
units.english: He that is endued with the intelligence maketh friendships with those that are wise, having first examined by the aid of his intelligence, repeatedly searching by his understanding, and using his ears, eyes, and judgment.

units.sanskrit: avṛttim vinayaḥ hanti hanti anartham parākramaḥ
units.english: Humility removeth obloquy, ears, failure, prowess;

units.sanskrit: hanti nityam kṣamā krodham ācāraḥ hanti alakṣaṇam
units.english: forgiveness always conquereth anger; and auspicious rites destroy all indications of evil.

units.sanskrit: paricchadena kṣetreṇa veśmanā paricaryayā parīkṣeta kulam rājan bhojana ācchādanena ca
units.english: One's lineage, O king, is tested by his objects of enjoyment, place of birth, house, behaviour, food, and dress.

units.sanskrit: upasthitasya kāmasya prativādaḥ na vidyate
units.english: When an object of enjoyment is available, even that one who hath attained emancipation is not unwilling to enjoy;

units.sanskrit: api nirmukta dehasya kāmaraktasya kim punar prājña upasevinam vaidyam dhārmikam priya darśanam mitravantam su vākyam ca suhṛdam paripālayet
units.english: what, again, need be said of him that is yet wedded to desire? A king should cherish a counsellor that worshippeth persons of wisdom, is endued with learning, virtue, agreeable appearance, friends, sweet speech, and a good heart.

units.sanskrit: duṣkulīnaḥ kulīnaḥ vā maryādām yaḥ na laṅghayet dharma apekṣī mṛduḥ hrīmān sa kulīna śatāt varaḥ
units.english: Whether of low or high birth, he who doth not transgress the rules of polite intercourse, who hath an eye on virtue, who is endued with humility and modesty, is superior to a hundred persons of high birth.

units.sanskrit: artha saṃtati kāmaḥ ca rakṣet etāni nityaśas
units.english: The friendship of those persons never cooleth, whose hearts, secret pursuits, and pleasures, and acquirements, accord in every respect.

units.sanskrit: durbuddhim akṛtaprajñam channam kūpam tṛṇaiḥ iva vivarjayīta medhāvī tasmin maitrī praṇaśyati
units.english: He that is intelligent should avoid an ignorant person of wicked soul, like a pit whose mouth is covered with grass, for friendship with such a person can never last.

units.sanskrit: avalipteṣu mūrkheṣu raudra sāhasikeṣu ca tathā eva apeta dharmeṣu na maitrīm ācaret budhaḥ
units.english: The man of wisdom should never contract friendship with those that are proud, ignorant, fierce, rash and fallen off from righteousness.

units.sanskrit: kṛtajñam dhārmikam satyam akṣudram dṛḍha bhaktikam jita indriyam sthitam sthityām mitram atyāgi ca iṣyate
units.english: He that is grateful, virtuous, truthful, large-hearted, and devoted, and he that hath his senses under control, preserveth his dignity, and never forsaketh a friend, should be desired for a friend.

units.sanskrit: indriyāṇām anutsargaḥ mṛtyunā na viśiṣyate
units.english: The withdrawal of the senses from their respective objects is equivalent to death itself.

units.sanskrit: atyartham punar utsargaḥ sādayet daivatāni api
units.english: Their excessive indulgence again would ruin the very gods.

units.sanskrit: mārdavam sarva bhūtānām anasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ āyuṣyāṇi budhāḥ prāhuḥ mitrāṇām ca avimānanā
units.english: Humility, love of all creatures, forgiveness, and respect for friends,--these, the learned have said, lengthen life.

units.sanskrit: apanītam su nītena yaḥ artham pratyāninīṣate matim āsthāya su dṛḍhām tat a kāpuruṣa vratam
units.english: He who with a firm resolution striveth to accomplish by a virtuous policy purposes that have once been frustrated, is said to possess real manhood.

units.sanskrit: āyatyām pratikāra jñaḥ tadātve dṛḍha niścayaḥ atīte kārya śeṣa jñaḥ naraḥ arthaiḥ na prahīyate
units.english: That man attaineth all his objects, who is conversant with remedies to be applied in the future, who is firmly resolved in the present, and who could anticipate in the past how an act begun would end.

units.sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā yat abhīkṣṇam niṣevate
units.english: That which a man pursueth in word, deed, and thought, winneth him for its own;

units.sanskrit: tat eva apaharati enam tasmāt kalyāṇam ācaret
units.english: therefore, one should always seek that which is for his good.

units.sanskrit: maṅgala ālambhanam yogaḥ śrutam utthānam ārjavam bhūtim etāni kurvanti satām ca abhīkṣṇa darśanam
units.english: Effort after securing what is good, the properties of time, place, and means, acquaintance with the scriptures, activity, straightforwardness, and frequent meetings with those that are good,--these bring about prosperity.

units.sanskrit: anirvedaḥ śriyaḥ mūlam duḥkha nāśe sukhasya ca
units.english: Perseverance is the root of prosperity, of gain, and of what is beneficial.

units.sanskrit: mahān bhavati anirviṇṇaḥ sukham ca atyantam aśnute
units.english: The man that pursueth an object with perseverance and without giving it up in vexation, is really great, and enjoyeth happiness that is unending.

units.sanskrit: na atas śrīmattaram kim cit anyat pathyatamam tathā
units.english: O sire, there is nothing more conducive of happiness and nothing more proper for a man of power and energy as foregiveness in every place and at all times.

units.sanskrit: prabhaviṣṇoḥ yathā tāta kṣamā sarvatra sarvadā
units.english: He that is weak should forgive under all circumstances.

units.sanskrit: kṣamet aśaktaḥ sarvasya śaktimān dharma kāraṇāt
units.english: He that is possessed of power should show forgiveness from motives of virtue;

units.sanskrit: artha anarthau samau yasya tasya nityam kṣamā hitā
units.english: and he, to whom the success or failure of his objects is the same, is naturally forgiving.

units.sanskrit: yat sukham sevamānaḥ api dharma arthābhyām na hīyate
units.english: That pleasure the pursuit of which doth not injure one's virtue and profit, should certainly be pursued to one's fill.

units.sanskrit: kāmam tat upaseveta na mūḍha vratam ācaret
units.english: One should not, however, act like a fool by giving free indulgence to his senses.

units.sanskrit: duḥkha ārteṣu pramatteṣu nāstikeṣu alaseṣu ca na śrīḥ vasati adānteṣu ye ca utsāha vivarjitāḥ
units.english: Prosperity never resides in one who suffers himself to be tortured by a grief, who is addicted to evil ways, who denies Godhead, who is idle, who hath not his senses under control, and who is divested of exertion.

units.sanskrit: ārjavena naram yuktam ārjavāt sa vyapatrapam aśaktimantam manyantaḥ dharṣayanti ku buddhayaḥ
units.english: The man that is humble, and who from humility is modest is regarded as weak and persecuted by persons of misdirected intelligence.

units.sanskrit: ati āryam atidātāram ati śūram ativratam prajñā abhimāninam ca eva śrīḥ bhayāt na upasarpati
units.english: Prosperity never approacheth from fear the person that is excessively liberal, that giveth away without measure, that is possessed of extraordinary bravery, that practiseth the most rigid vows, and that is very proud of his wisdom.

units.sanskrit: na ca ati guṇavatsu eṣā na atyantam nirguṇeṣu ca
units.english: Prosperity doth not reside in one that is highly accomplished, nor in one that is without any accomplishment.

units.sanskrit: na eṣā guṇān kāmayate nairguṇyāt na anurajyate
units.english: She doth not desire a combination of all the virtues, nor is she pleased with the total absence of all virtues.

units.sanskrit: unmattā gauḥ iva andhā śrīḥ kva cit eva avatiṣṭhate
units.english: Blind, like a mad cow, prosperity resides with some one who is not remarkable.

units.sanskrit: agnihotra phalāḥ vedāḥ śīla vṛtta phalam śrutam
units.english: The fruits of the Vedas are ceremonies performed before the (homa) fire; the fruits of an acquaintance with the scriptures are goodness of disposition and conduct.

units.sanskrit: rati putra phalāḥ dārāḥ datta bhukta phalam dhanam
units.english: The fruits of women are the pleasures of intercourse and offspring; and the fruits of wealth are enjoyment and charity.

units.sanskrit: adharma upārjitaiḥ arthaiḥ yaḥ karoti aurdhvadehikam na sa tasya phalam pretya bhuṅkte arthasya durāgamāt
units.english: He that performeth acts tending to secure his prosperity in the other world with wealth acquired sinfully, never reapeth the fruits of these acts in the other world, in consequence of the sinfulness of the acquisitions (spent for the purpose).

units.sanskrit: kāntāra vana durgeṣu kṛcchrāsu āpatsu saṃbhrame udyateṣu ca śastreṣu na asti śeṣavatām bhayam
units.english: In the midst of deserts, or deep woods, or inaccessible fastnesses, amid all kinds of dangers and alarms or in view of deadly weapons upraised for striking him, he that hath strength of mind entertaineth no fear.

units.sanskrit: utthānam saṃyamaḥ dākṣyam apramādaḥ dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ samīkṣya ca samārambhaḥ viddhi mūlam bhavasya tat
units.english: Exertion, self-control, skill, carefulness, steadiness, memory, and commencement of acts after mature deliberation,--know that these are the roots of prosperity.

units.sanskrit: tapaḥ balam tāpasānām brahma brahma vidām balam
units.english: Austerities constitute the strength of ascetics; the Vedas are the strength of those conversant with them;

units.sanskrit: hiṃsā balam asādhūnām kṣamā guṇavatām balam
units.english: in envy lieth the strength of the wicked; and in forgiveness, the strength of the virtuous.

units.sanskrit: aṣṭau tāni avrata ghnāni āpaḥ mūlam phalam payaḥ haviḥ brāhmaṇa kāmyā ca guroḥ vacanam auṣadham
units.english: These eight, viz., water, roots, fruits, milk, clarified butter (what is done at) the desire of a Brahmana, (or at) the command of a preceptor, and medicine, are not destructive of a vow.

units.sanskrit: na tat parasya saṃdadhyāt pratikūlam yadā ātmanaḥ
units.english: That which is antagonistic to one's own self, should never be applied in respect of another.

units.sanskrit: saṃgraheṇa eṣa dharmaḥ syāt kāmāt anyaḥ pravartate
units.english: Other kinds of virtue there are, but these proceed from caprice.

units.sanskrit: akrodhena jayet krodham asādhum sādhunā jayet
units.english: Anger must be conquered by forgiveness; and the wicked must be conquered by honesty;

units.sanskrit: jayet kadaryam dānena jayet satyena ca anṛtam
units.english: the miser must be conquered by liberality, and falsehood must be conquered by truth.

units.sanskrit: strī dhūrtake alase bhīrau caṇḍe puruṣa mānini caure kṛtaghne viśvāsaḥ na kāryaḥ na ca nāstike
units.english: One should not place trust on a woman, a swindler, an idle person, a coward, one that is fierce, one that boasts of his own power, a thief, an ungrateful person, and an atheist.

units.sanskrit: abhivādana śīlasya nityam vṛddha upasevinaḥ catvāri saṃpravardhante kīrtiḥ āyuḥ yaśaḥ balam
units.english: Achievements, period of life, fame, and power--these four always expand in the case of him that respectfully saluteth his superiors and waiteth upon the old.

units.sanskrit: atikleśena ye arthāḥ syuḥ dharmasya atikrameṇa ca areḥ vā praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ
units.english: Do not set thy heart after these objects which cannot be acquired except by very painful exertion, or by sacrificing righteousness, or by bowing down to an enemy.

units.sanskrit: avidyaḥ puruṣaḥ śocyaḥ śocyam mithunam aprajam
units.english: A man without knowledge is to be pitied;

units.sanskrit: nirāhārāḥ prajāḥ śocyāḥ śocyam rāṣṭram arājakam
units.english: the people of a kingdom that are without food are to be pitied; and a kingdom without a king is to be pitied. These constitute the source of pain and weakness to embodied creatures;

units.sanskrit: adhvā jarā dehavatām parvatānām jalam jarā
units.english: the rains, decay of hills and mountains;

units.sanskrit: asaṃbhogaḥ jarā strīṇām vāc śalyam manasaḥ jarā
units.english: absence of enjoyment, anguish of women;

units.sanskrit: anāmnāya malāḥ vedāḥ brāhmaṇasya avratam malam
units.english: The scum of the Vedas is want of study; of Brahmanas, absence of vows;

units.sanskrit: malam pṛthivyāḥ vāhīkāḥ puruṣasya anṛtam malam
units.english: of the Earth, the Vahlikas; of man, untruth;

units.sanskrit: kautūhala malā sādhvī vipra vāsa malāḥ striyaḥ
units.english: of the chaste woman, curiosity;

units.sanskrit: suvarṇasya malam rūpyam rūpyasya api malam trapu
units.english: The scum of gold is silver; of silver, tin; of tin, lead;

units.sanskrit: jñeyam trapu malam sīsam sīsasya api malam malam
units.english: and of lead, useless dross.

units.sanskrit: na svapnena jayet nidrām na kāmena striyam jayet
units.english: One cannot conquer sleep by lying down; women by desire;
