units.sanskrit: na indhanena jayet agnim na pānena surām jayet
units.english: fire by fuel; and wine by drinking.

units.sanskrit: yasya dāna jitam mitram amitrāḥ yudhi nirjitāḥ anna pāna jitāḥ dārāḥ saphalam tasya jīvitam
units.english: His life is, indeed, crowned with success who hath won his friends by gifts, his foes in battle, and wife by food and drink;

units.sanskrit: sahasriṇaḥ api jīvanti jīvanti śatinaḥ tathā
units.english: they who have thousands live; they, who have hundreds, also live.

units.sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭram vimuñca icchām na katham cit na jīvyate
units.english: O Dhritarashtra, forsake desire. There is none who cannot manage to live by some means or other.

units.sanskrit: yat pṛthivyām vrīhi yavam hiraṇyam paśavaḥ striyaḥ na alam ekasya tat sarvam iti paśyan na muhyati
units.english: Thy paddy, wheat, gold, animals, and women that are on earth all cannot satiate even one person ..

units.sanskrit: rājan bhūyas bravīmi tvām putreṣu samam ācara samatā yadi te rājan sveṣu pāṇḍu suteṣu ca viduraḥ uvāca
units.english: O king, I again tell thee, adopt an equal conduct towards thy children, i.e., towards the sons of Pandu and thy own sons.'" SECTION XL "Vidura said, 'Worshipped by the good and abandoning pride, that good man who pursueth his objects without outstepping the limits of his power, soon succeedeth in winning fame, for they that are good, when gratified with a person, are certainly competent to bestow happiness on him.

units.sanskrit: mahāntam api artham adharma yuktam yaḥ saṃtyajati an upākruṣṭaḥ eva sukham sa duḥkhāni avamucya śete
units.english: He that forsaketh, of his own accord, even a great object owing to its being fraught with unrighteousness, liveth happily, casting off all foes, like a snake that hath cast off its slough.

units.sanskrit: anṛtam ca samutkarṣe rāja gāmi ca paiśunam guroḥ ca alīka nirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā
units.english: A victory gained by an untruth, deceitful conduct towards the king, and insincerity of intentions expressed before the preceptor,--these three are each equal to the sin of slaying a Brahmana.

units.sanskrit: asūyā eka padam mṛtyuḥ ativādaḥ śriyaḥ vadhaḥ
units.english: Excessive envy, death, and boastfulness, are the causes of the destruction of prosperity.

units.sanskrit: a śuśrūṣā tvarā ślāghā vidyāyāḥ śatravaḥ trayaḥ
units.english: Carelessness in waiting upon preceptor, haste, and boastlessness, are the three enemies of knowledge.

units.sanskrit: ālasyam mada mohau ca cāpalam goṣṭhiḥ eva ca stabdha tā ca abhimāni tvam tathā atyāgi tvam eva ca ete vai sapta doṣāḥ tu sadā vidyā arthinām matāḥ
units.english: Idleness, inattention, confusion of the intellect, restlessness, gathering for killing time, haughtiness, pride, and covetous ness,--these seven constitute, it is said, the faults of students in the pursuit of learning.

units.sanskrit: sukha arthinaḥ kutas vidyā na asti vidyā arthinaḥ sukham
units.english: How can they that desire pleasure have knowledge? Students, again, engaged in the pursuit of learning, cannot have pleasure.

units.sanskrit: sukha arthī vā tyajet vidyām vidyā arthī vā sukham tyajet
units.english: Votaries of pleasure must give up knowledge, and votaries of knowledge must give up pleasure.

units.sanskrit: na agniḥ tṛpyati kāṣṭhānām na āpagānām mahā udadhiḥ
units.english: Fire is never gratified with fuel (but can consume any measure thereof). The great ocean is never gratified with the rivers it receives (but can receive any number of them).

units.sanskrit: na antakaḥ sarva bhūtānām na puṃsām vāma locanā
units.english: Death is never gratified even with entire living creatures.

units.sanskrit: āśāḥ dhṛtim hanti samṛddhim antakaḥ
units.english: O king, hope killeth patience;

units.sanskrit: krodhaḥ śriyam hanti yaśaḥ kadarya tā
units.english: anger killeth prosperity; miserliness killeth fame;

units.sanskrit: a pālanam hanti paśūn ca rājan
units.english: absence of tending killeth cattle;

units.sanskrit: ekaḥ kruddhaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ hanti rāṣṭram
units.english: one angry Brahmana destroyeth a whole kingdom.

units.sanskrit: vṛddhaḥ jñātiḥ avasannaḥ vayasya etāni te santu gṛhe sadā eva aja ukṣā candanam vīṇā ādarśaḥ madhu sarpiṣī
units.english: Let goats, brass, silver, honey, antidotes of poison, birds, Brahmanas versed in the Vedas, old relatives, and men of high birth sunk in poverty, be always present in thy house.

units.sanskrit: gṛhe sthāpayitavyāni dhanyāni manuḥ abravīt
units.english: O Bharata, Manu hath said that goats, bulls, sandal, lyres, mirrors, honey, clarified butter, iron, copper, conch-shells, salagram (the stony-image of Vishnu with gold within) and gorochana should always be kept in one's house for the worship of the gods.

units.sanskrit: deva brāhmaṇa pūjā artham atithīnām ca bhārata
units.english: Brahmanas, and guests, for all those objects are auspicious.

units.sanskrit: idam ca tvām sarva param bravīmi puṇyam padam tāta mahā viśiṣṭam na jātu kāmāt na bhayāt na lobhāt
units.english: O sire, I would impart to thee another sacred lesson productive of great fruits, and which is the highest of all teachings, viz., virtue should never be forsaken from desire, fear, or temptation, nay, nor for the sake of life itself.

units.sanskrit: nityaḥ dharmaḥ sukha duḥkhe tu anitye
units.english: Virtue is everlasting; pleasure and pain are transitory;

units.sanskrit: nityaḥ jīvaḥ dhātuḥ asya tu anityaḥ
units.english: life is, indeed, everlasting but its particular phases are transitory.

units.sanskrit: tyaktvā anityam pratitiṣṭhasva nitye saṃtuṣya tvam toṣa paraḥ hi lābhaḥ
units.english: Forsaking those which are transitory, betake thyself to that which is everlasting, and let contentment be thine, for contentment is the highest of all acquisitions.

units.sanskrit: mahā balān paśya mahā anubhāvān praśāsya bhūmim dhana dhānya pūrṇām rājyāni hitvā vipulān ca bhogān
units.english: Behold, illustrious and mighty kings, having ruled lands abounding with wealth and corn, have become the victims of the Universal Destroyer, leaving behind their kingdoms and vast sources of enjoyment.

units.sanskrit: mṛtam putram duḥkha puṣṭam manuṣyā
units.english: The son brought up with anxious care, when dead, is taken up and carried away by men (to the burning ground).

units.sanskrit: utkṣipya rājan sva gṛhāt nirharanti tam mukta keśāḥ karuṇam rudantaḥ citā madhye kāṣṭham iva kṣipanti
units.english: With the dishevelled hair and crying piteously, they then cast the body into the funeral pyre, as if it were a piece of wood.

units.sanskrit: anyaḥ dhanam preta gatasya bhuṅkte vayāṃsi ca agniḥ ca śarīra dhātūn
units.english: Others enjoy the deceased's wealth, while birds and fire feast on the elements of his body.

units.sanskrit: dvābhyām ayam saha gacchati amutra puṇyena pāpena ca veṣṭyamānaḥ
units.english: With two only he goeth to the other world, viz., his merits and his sins which keep him company.

units.sanskrit: utsṛjya vinivartante jñātayaḥ suhṛdaḥ sutāḥ apuṣpān aphalān vṛkṣān yathā tāta patatriṇaḥ
units.english: Throwing away the body, O sire, relatives, friends, and sons retrace their steps, like birds abandoning trees without blossoms and fruits.

units.sanskrit: agnau prāstam tu puruṣam karma anveti svayaṃkṛtam
units.english: The person cast into the funeral pyre is followed only by his own acts.

units.sanskrit: tasmāt tu puruṣaḥ yatnāt dharmam saṃcinuyāt śanais
units.english: Therefore, should men carefully and gradually earn the merit of righteousness.

units.sanskrit: asmāt lokāt ūrdhvam amuṣya ca adho mahat tamaḥ tiṣṭhati hi andhakāram
units.english: In the world above this, and also in that below this, there are regions of great gloom and darkness.

units.sanskrit: tat vai mahā mohanam indriyāṇām
units.english: Know, O king, that those are regions where the senses of men are exceedingly afflicted.

units.sanskrit: budhyasva mā tvām pralabheta rājan
units.english: Oh, let not any of those places to thine.

units.sanskrit: niśamya sarvam pratipattum evam yaśaḥ param prāpsyasi jīva loke bhayam na ca amutra na ca iha te asti
units.english: Carefully listening to these words, if thou canst act according to them, thou wilt obtain great fame in this world of men, and fear will not be thine here or hereafter.

units.sanskrit: ātmā nadī bhārata puṇya tīrthā
units.english: O Bharata, the soul is spoken of as a river; religious merit constitutes its sacred baths;

units.sanskrit: satya udakā dhṛti kūlā dama ūrmiḥ
units.english: truth, its water; self-control, its banks; kindness, its waves.

units.sanskrit: tasyām snātaḥ pūyate puṇya karmā puṇyaḥ hi ātmā nityam ambhaḥ ambhaḥ eva
units.english: He that is righteous purifieth himself by a bath therein, for the soul is sacred, and the absence of desire is the highest merit.

units.sanskrit: kāma krodha grāhavatīm pañca indriya jalām nadīm kṛtvā dhṛti mayīm nāvam janma durgāṇi saṃtara
units.english: O king, life is a river whose waters are the five senses, and whose crocodiles and sharks are desire and anger.

units.sanskrit: prajñā vṛddham dharma vṛddham sva bandhum vidyā vṛddham vayasā ca api vṛddham kārya akārye pūjayitvā prasādya
units.english: Making self-control thy raft, cross thou its eddies which are represented by repeated births! Worshipping and gratifying friends that are eminent in wisdom, virtue, learning, and years, he that asketh their advice about what he should do and should not do, is never misled.

units.sanskrit: dhṛtyā śiśna udaram rakṣet pāṇi pādam ca cakṣuṣā
units.english: One should restrain one's lust and stomach by patience; one's hands and feet by one's eyes;

units.sanskrit: cakṣuḥ śrotre ca manasā manaḥ vācam ca karmaṇā
units.english: one's eyes and ears by one's mind; and one's mind and words by one's acts.

units.sanskrit: nitya svādhyāyī patita anna varjī ṛtam bruvan gurave karma kurvan na brāhmaṇaḥ cyavate brahma lokāt
units.english: That Brahmana who never omitteth to perform his ablutions, who always weareth his sacred thread, who always attendeth to the study of the Vedas, who always avoideth food that is unclean, who telleth the truth and performeth acts in honour of his preceptor, never falleth off from the region of Brahma.

units.sanskrit: iṣṭvā yajñaiḥ pālayitvā prajāḥ ca go brāhmaṇa arthe śastra pūta antarātmā hataḥ saṃgrāme kṣatriyaḥ svargam eti
units.english: Having studied the Vedas, poured libations into fire, performed sacrifices, protected subjects, sanctified his soul by drawing weapons for protecting kine and Brahmanas, and died on the field of battle, the Kshatriya attaineth to heaven.

units.sanskrit: vaiśyaḥ adhītya brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān ca dhanaiḥ kāle saṃvibhajya āśritān ca tretā pūtam dhūmam āghrāya puṇyam
units.english: Having studied the Vedas, and distributed in proper time, his wealth among Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and his own dependents, and inhaled the sanctified smoke of the three kinds of fires, the Vaisya enjoyeth heavenly bliss in the other world.

units.sanskrit: pretya svarge deva sukhāni bhuṅkte brahma kṣatram vaiśya varṇam ca śūdraḥ krameṇa etān nyāyataḥ pūjayānaḥ
units.english: Having properly worshipped Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaisayas in due order, and having burnt his sins, by gratifying them, and then peacefully casting off his body, the Sudra enjoyeth the bliss of heaven.

units.sanskrit: cāturvarṇyasya eṣa dharmaḥ tava uktaḥ
units.english: The duties of the four orders are thus set forth before thee.

units.sanskrit: hetum ca atra bruvataḥ me nibodha
units.english: Listen now to the reason of my speech as I discourse it.

units.sanskrit: kṣātrāt dharmāt dhīyate pāṇḍu putraḥ
units.english: Yudhishthira, the son of Pandu, is falling off from the duties of the Kshatriya order.

units.sanskrit: tam tvam rājan rāja dharme niyuṅkṣva dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ uvāca evam etat yathā mām tvam anuśāsasi nityadā
units.english: Place him, therefore, O king, in a position to discharge the duties of kings.' "Dhritarashtra said, It is even so as thou always teachest me.

units.sanskrit: mama api ca matiḥ saumya bhavati evam yathā āttha mām
units.english: O amiable one, my heart also inclineth that very way of which thou tellest me.

units.sanskrit: sā tu buddhiḥ kṛtā api evam pāṇḍavān prati me sadā duryodhanam samāsādya punar viparivartate
units.english: Although, however, I incline in my mind towards the Pandavas even as thou teachest me to do, yet as soon as I come in contact with Duryodhana it turneth off in a different way.

units.sanskrit: na diṣṭam abhyatikrāntum śakyam martyena kena cit
units.english: No creature is able to avert fate.

units.sanskrit: diṣṭam eva kṛtam manye pauruṣam tu nirarthakam
units.english: Indeed, Destiny, I think, is certain to take its course;
